import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from './Avatar' import * as AvatarStories from './Avatar.stories' # Avatar A picture of a person or account, with initials or a silhouette when there is no picture, an optional presence dot, and a group that overlaps several. ## Variants Neutral by default. `color` picks any accent hue, and `variant` how strong it is. Behind a photo the colour only shows while it loads or where the image is transparent. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `subtle` | Most places: lists, comments, a byline. A tint that sits quietly next to text. | | `solid` | Where the avatar has to stand out on its own: a header, an account menu trigger. | Colour tells people apart in a list; it carries no meaning. Pick it from the person (a hash of their id), never from a status. ### Sizes Atlassian's six. `md` is the default. | `size` | Across | Use for | | --- | --- | --- | | `xs` | 16px | Inline with a line of small text: a mention, a dense table cell. One initial. | | `sm` | 24px | Beside a name in a row, a field or a table cell. | | `md` | 32px | The default: a comment, a feed event, the account button in a top bar. | | `lg` | 40px | The leading visual of a list row or a card. | | `xl` | 96px | A profile header. | | `2xl` | 128px | A profile page, or the picture being edited. | With initials, `xs` shows the first letter only: two do not fit in 16px. ### Status `status` puts a presence dot on the bottom-end corner, in Badge's presence colours: online, away, busy, offline. The dot grows with the avatar, and at `xl` and `2xl` it sits on the curve: ### Group `AvatarGroup` overlaps a row of avatars, for the people on a record or a thread. `max` is the most circles in the row, the "+n" included. With `hasTooltips`, each named avatar shows its name on hover, and the "+n" lists the people it stands for, on hover or keyboard focus: ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from 'zweihander/avatar' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/avatar.json ``` - Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Avatar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Avatar.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/avatar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/avatar) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy One avatar shows one of image, initials or silhouette, in that order of preference. A broken image falls back to the next. The status dot and the group are optional. ## Measurements The circle ignores the Theme's radius preset: a circle is the shape, not a corner setting. The image fills the circle edge to edge. The silhouette is the kit's `user` icon at 60% of the circle, centred. Initials are 12px up to `md`, where `xs` keeps only the first letter, 14px on `lg`, then 28px and 32px: the type scale stops at 32px, so on `xl` and `2xl` the letters are a smaller share of the circle. They are medium (500) up to `lg` and semibold (600) on `xl` and `2xl`, Figma's Heading/xl and Heading/2xl. An `xs` avatar draws no status dot, as in Atlassian: at 16px the dot would cover most of the picture, so the status is in the accessible name only. The status dot is an 8px Badge dot (`md`) on the sm, md and lg avatars, flush on the corner of the avatar's box, outside the curve. On `xl` and `2xl` that corner is far off the circle and a Badge dot is a speck, so the dot is 16px and 20px, and its centre sits on the circle at 45°. The ring is 2px at every size, as on a floating Badge. The overlap is Atlassian's: 4px, and none at `sm`, where the 24px circles only touch. ## Color `color` sets the Theme's own `data-accent` on the avatar, so a hue avatar reads the accent tokens of that hue: switch the accent in the toolbar to see the values for another one. The status dot takes Badge's presence colours: online `success`, away `warning`, busy `destructive`, offline `secondary`. The "+n" in a group is a neutral subtle avatar. ## States An avatar is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. Its states are which part it can show. }, { label: 'Initials', content: }, { label: 'Silhouette', content: }, { label: 'Broken image', content: }, { label: 'Online', content: }, { label: 'Offline', content: }, ]} /> - **Image** shows while `imageSrc` loads and after. - **Broken image** drops the `` and shows the initials, or the silhouette when there are none, instead of the browser's broken-image icon. A new `imageSrc` is tried again. An empty `imageSrc` is no image. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `` attribute passes through to the container, including `ref`. ### AvatarGroup
Every other `` attribute passes through to the row. ### Differences from the spec - **`initials` is added.** The spec's Anatomy has an Initials part but its prop list has no way to set them. Pass the letters, not a name: how to abbreviate a name depends on the language, and the kit should not guess. - **A broken image falls back** to initials or the silhouette instead of showing the browser's broken-image icon. - **Sizes follow Atlassian Design**: 16, 24, 32, 40, 96 and 128px, with `md` (32px) the default, so an avatar lines up with the kit's 32px controls. There is no 48px. - **`xs` shows one initial.** Two letters do not fit in 16px at the smallest type size. - **No square, no `appearance`.** Always a circle, so a person never reads as a product or workspace logo. - **The placeholder is the kit's `user` icon** at 60% of the circle, centred, as in Figma. It takes `color` and `variant` like initials do. - **`color` and `variant` are added**, to tell people apart in a list. - **The circle ignores the radius preset.** - **`status` and `AvatarGroup` are added.** The status words and the "+n" name are English by default; `statusLabel` and `moreLabel` translate them. - **`max` counts the "+n".** The row never grows past `max` circles, and the "+n" always stands for two or more: never "+1" where the person would have fitted. ## When to use Use an Avatar to show who: the author of a comment, the people on a project, the account that is signed in. Give it `imageAlt` when the avatar is the only thing that says who it is. When the name is printed next to it, leave `imageAlt` out: the avatar is decorative, and the name is read once. } doCaption="The name is printed, so the avatar has no imageAlt. A screen reader hears “Mary Thompson” once." dont={} dontCaption="imageAlt repeats the printed name: “Mary Thompson, image, Mary Thompson”." /> ## When not to use - **For a product, team or workspace logo.** An Avatar is always round, so it reads as a person. Use an image with its own shape. - **For status through colour.** The avatar's `color` means nothing. Use `status` for presence, and print the status where people act on it (an assignee picker): a dot is a glance, not the only cue. - **For a long list of people.** A group shows who at a glance; past a handful, show the count or a list of names instead. - **For an icon in a circle.** Use the icon itself, or an icon-only [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) when it acts. ## Accessibility - `imageAlt` names the **whole avatar** (`role="img"`), not just the image, so the image, the initials and the silhouette all announce the same person. The inner `` has `alt=""`. - Without `imageAlt` the avatar is **decorative** and hidden (`aria-hidden`), its status dot with it. - With `status`, the status **joins the name**: "Mary Thompson, Online". The dot itself is not read. - In a group, the "+n" is named "3 more" when the avatars are named, and decorative when they are not. - With `hasTooltips`, the "+n" is the one avatar that takes focus, with the focus ring, and its tooltip of hidden names is its description. The other avatars' tooltips open on hover only: their names are already their accessible names. - Initials are never read out: with `imageAlt` the avatar's name replaces them, without it the avatar is hidden. They are uppercased with CSS, so the text keeps the letters as passed. - Initials meet 4.5:1 in every colour and variant, on every gray ramp in both modes, measured by the `Contrast` story. Neutral solid is gray 600 under gray 50, 6.5:1 or more. - The silhouette uses the initials colour (neutral subtle uses `--color-text-subtlest`), past the 3:1 a graphic needs in every colour and variant, measured by the `Contrast` story.

components-atomic-elements-badge--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Badge } from './Badge' import * as BadgeStories from './Badge.stories' # Badge A small count or dot that flags something new on another element: unread messages on an inbox, a status on an avatar. ## Variants Each variant comes as a count or, with `isDot`, a dot. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `primary` | The default: new items in the brand colour. | | `accent` | Strong and neutral, where the brand colour would clash. | | `secondary` | Low emphasis: a total, not news. As a dot, Offline. | | `destructive` | Something needs attention: failures, overdue items. As a dot, Busy. | | `success` | As a dot, Online. | | `warning` | As a dot, Away or Pending. | `maxCount` keeps a large number from stretching the badge past its anchor. `isFloating` pins the badge to a corner of the element it wraps. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Badge } from 'zweihander/badge' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/badge.json ``` - Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Badge.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Badge.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/badge](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/badge) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The anchor only exists when the badge has `children`. A badge on its own is just the container. ## Measurements One count badge, Atlassian's: 16px tall and at least 24px wide, so a column of one- and two-digit counts lines up. `size` picks the dot: 8px (`md`) or 6px (`sm`). `size="sm"` on a count is deprecated. It renders the same badge as `md` and warns once in development; in the next release `sm` is for dots only. `size="md"` on a count, the default written out, and `sm` on a dot are silent. A floating badge is centred on its corner of the anchor, half in and half out, with a 2px ring. ## Color A dot has no text to carry it, so it must reach 3:1 against the page on its own. That is why the `secondary` and `warning` dots step to a darker colour than their count badge. ## States A badge is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. Its states are what it shows. }, { label: 'Over maxCount', content: }, { label: 'Zero', content: }, { label: 'Dot', content: }, ]} /> `count={0}` shows "0". Hide the badge yourself if nothing new should mean no badge. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `` attribute passes through to the badge, not to the anchor. ### Differences from the spec - **Atlassian's box, not a pill.** A count is 16px tall, at least 24px wide, with a 2px corner, in one size. Only the dot is round. - **`children` is added.** A floating badge needs something to float on. The badge wraps it in a `position: relative` span rather than asking every consumer to position the anchor themselves. - **`accent` is the inverted neutral.** The token set has one brand hue, which `primary` already uses, so `accent` is foreground-on-background: the strongest contrast available without inventing a colour. - **`success` and `warning` are added** from the status tokens, for presence and state dots. - **`floatingPlacement` defaults to `top-end`**, the usual notification corner; the spec gives no default. - **Start and end are physical** (left and right). RTL pages would get mirrored placement. ## When to use Use a Badge to say something is new, or how many, on the element it belongs to: unread messages on an inbox button, a status dot on an avatar. A floating badge is hidden from assistive tech, so the element it sits on carries the meaning in its own name. } doCaption="The button is named “Notifications, 4 unread”: the count reaches a screen reader too." dont={} dontCaption="The count lives only in the badge, which is hidden: a screen reader hears “Notifications”." /> Colour is never the only signal. A destructive badge still needs words somewhere that say what is wrong, and a status dot needs `aria-label` or a name beside it. ## When not to use - **For a label or category.** Use a [Tag](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-tag--docs): it holds words, a badge holds a number. - **For a message that needs reading.** Use an Alert or a Toast. - **On every item of a list.** A badge flags what is new; if everything is, nothing stands out. ## Accessibility - An **inline count** is plain text and is read where it sits. Inside a button it becomes part of the name ("Inbox 12"). - A **floating** badge is hidden from assistive tech: it sits *outside* the element it decorates, so it would be read as a stray number after it. Put the meaning in that element's name instead: `aria-label="Notifications, 4 unread"`. - A **dot** has no text and is hidden too. - Pass `aria-label` to any badge to expose it as an image with that name instead, e.g. a status dot on an avatar: `aria-label="Online"`. - Contrast is checked by addon-a11y in error mode for every story.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Divider } from './Divider' import * as DividerStories from './Divider.stories' export const Stack = ({ children }) => (
Above {children} Below
) # Divider A thin line that separates content into groups: sections of a card, items in a toolbar, blocks of a page. ## Variants | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | `solid` | Almost everywhere: the quiet default. | | `dashed` | A boundary that is softer or provisional: a drop zone, a "more below" break, a draft section. | A **vertical** divider separates items in a row: toolbar groups, links in a footer. It has no fixed height and stretches to its flex row. **Inset** stops the line short of the container's edges, so it aligns with the text in a padded list rather than running edge to edge. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Divider } from 'zweihander/divider' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/divider.json ``` - Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Divider.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Divider.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/divider](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/divider) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy One part. The line is a border, top for horizontal and start for vertical, and the box shrinks to it: a vertical divider is exactly as wide as its line. ## Measurements Thickness is whole pixels, not a token: `--border-width` covers 1px and `--border-width-selected` 2px, and a divider's three weights stay its own. | Size | Thickness | | --- | --- | | `sm` | 1px | | `md` | 2px | | `lg` | 4px | ## Color Every size and appearance uses the same colour. ## States A divider is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. It looks the same whether it is announced or decorative; only a screen reader tells them apart. }, { label: 'Dashed', content: }, { label: 'Inset', content: }, { label: 'Decorative', content: }, ]} /> ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through, including `ref` and `aria-hidden`. ### Differences from the spec - **`appearance`, not `variant`.** In this kit `variant` always means a colour by intent (primary, destructive…) and `appearance` means a style. Solid versus dashed is a style. - **Thickness is raw px.** `--border-width` and `--border-width-selected` cover 1px and 2px strokes; a divider is the only component that needs a third, so its three weights stay its own. ## When to use Use a Divider between groups that spacing alone does not separate: the sections of a menu, the blocks of a settings page, groups in a toolbar. Divide groups, not every item: a line after each row turns a list into stripes and makes the real breaks harder to see. } doCaption="One line between two groups: the break carries meaning." dont={} dontCaption="A line after every item: nothing stands out as a group." /> ## When not to use - **Where space already separates.** Cards, list items with padding and headed sections are grouped by their own whitespace; a line adds noise. - **As the only thing that tells groups apart.** The line is faint on purpose (see Accessibility). Pair it with a heading or space. - **For a border of a component.** Draw that with the component's own border, not a Divider beside it. ## Accessibility - `

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Tag } from './Tag' import * as TagStories from './Tag.stories' # Tag A short label that categorises or marks something: a status, a filter chip, a person picked in a field. ## Variants `variant` is the colour: a status, or a hue for categories. `appearance` is the emphasis. Any variant takes any appearance. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | | A plain label with no status: a type, a version. | | | Informational status: In review, Scheduled. The default. | | | Done or healthy: Paid, Verified, Live. | | | Needs attention soon: Expiring, Pending. | | | Failed or blocked: Overdue, Error. | | | A hue: one per category, label or owner. It carries no meaning. | | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | | Most places: a tint that sits in a row of text. | | | Dense tables and busy surfaces, where many tints would be loud. | | | One tag that must stand out: a single status on a card. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Tag } from 'zweihander/tag' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tag.json ``` - Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Tag.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Tag.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/tag](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tag) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy ## Measurements One size, Atlassian's tag: 20px tall, control tier xs (Foundations / Sizing), so it sits in a line of text. The border is always there, transparent unless outlined, so appearances never shift the layout. In a line of text the tag is centred on the line, whatever the text's size or family (the tag's own text is always the kit's sans; a mono table cell around it changes nothing): a 20px line of body text stays 20px with a tag in it (so a Table row stays 28px), and a taller line, like a heading's, keeps its height. Only a line shorter than the tag, 12/16 small text, grows to 20px. `size` is deprecated and the prop will be removed in the next release. `size="sm"` renders the same tag as `md` and warns once in development; `size="md"`, the default written out, is silent. | Part | Property | Value | | --- | --- | --- | | Container | Maximum width | 180px | The maximum width is Atlassian's and has no token: no size step is that wide. Past it, and past the width of its parent, the text ends in an ellipsis. The corner is 4px and follows the Theme's radius preset like every control: a pill under `radius="full-rounded"`. ## Color Each variant has a solid, a colour on that solid, a subtle tint and a text colour that subtle and outlined use. Subtle and outlined text is measured at 4.5:1 by the token build. Every hue follows the same four tokens under its own name. Red, as an example; the other sixteen swap `red` for their hue. ## States The tag itself is not interactive. Its remove button is: - **Hover** tints the button with the tag's own text colour at 15%, so it reads on every variant and appearance without a token for each. - **Focus** is the `--color-border-focused` outline every control uses, drawn inset so it stays inside a 20px tag. - Pressing removes nothing by itself: `onRemove` reports it, and the parent drops the tag from its list. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `` attribute passes through to the container, including `ref`. ### Differences from the spec - **The spec's four variants needed new tokens.** `info`, `success`, `warning` and `danger` were added to the token layer for Tag and are shared with Alert and Toast. - **One size.** The spec's sizes are gone: the tag takes Atlassian's box, 20px tall with 12/16 text and a 180px maximum width. `size` stays one release as a deprecated prop that changes nothing. - **No `isRounded`.** The corner reads the control tier's radius, so it follows the Theme's radius preset with every other control, and turns into a pill under `radius="full-rounded"`. - **The 17 hue variants are additions.** Solid is step 600 with a white label on every hue, in both appearances, so a row of solid tags reads as one set; on the warm hues (orange, amber, yellow, lime and others) that label falls below 4.5:1. That is accepted on purpose. - **`startAvatar` wins over `startIcon`** if both are passed; the spec does not say. - **Digits are tabular.** Every digit takes the same width, so a tag holding a count or a countdown does not change width as it ticks. - **The tag does not remove itself.** `onRemove` reports the click and the parent drops the tag from its list, so the list stays the one source of truth. ## When to use Use a Tag to label or categorise: a status on a row, the categories of an item, the filters applied to a list, the people picked in a field. Where a tag has to pass AA, use `subtle` or `outlined`: solid hue tags keep one white label across hues, which the warm ones carry under 4.5:1. } doCaption="Warm hues in subtle: every label clears 4.5:1." dont={} dontCaption="The same hues solid: the white label falls under 4.5:1." /> Colour carries meaning here, so it is never the only signal: the text says what the status is. In a wrapped list of removable tags on touch, keep at least `--space-6` between rows. The remove button's touch area reaches 12px above and below a 20px tag, and neighbouring targets would overlap. ## When not to use - **For an action.** A tag is a label; its only control is remove. Use a [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs). - **For a choice the user toggles on and off.** Use a [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) or a Checkbox. - **For a count.** Use a [Badge](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-badge--docs). ## Accessibility - The remove button is named **"Remove `text`"** (e.g. "Remove Design"), so a list of tags does not read as a row of identical "Remove" buttons. - It is a native `

Any variant takes any appearance. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | | The next step: Save, Continue, Create. One per view. | | | A strong action in neutral black or white, where the brand colour would clash or already means something else. | | | Everything else: Cancel, Back, Export. | | | Deleting, or anything that cannot be undone. | | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | | The action to take, filled so it is found first. | | | Actions that matter but are not the next step. | | | Low emphasis and dense places: toolbars, table rows, a card's corner. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Button } from 'zweihander/button' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/button.json ``` - Source: [src/components/buttons/Button.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/buttons/Button.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/button](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/button) - Behaviour: [Base UI Button](https://base-ui.com/react/components/button) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy While `isLoading`, a spinner takes the content's place; the content stays, invisible, so the button keeps its width and its name. ## Measurements Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing), with Atlassian Design's numbers: 32px by default, 24px for tables and dense rows. Buttons take the spacious inline padding, 12px at both sizes: a centred label needs more room either side than a field's left-aligned text. The 12px is measured from the button's outer edge to its label or icon, border included, as in Atlassian Design, and is the same with or without an icon on that side; icon and label sit 6px apart. Ghost has no border, so it is 11px from edge to label, as Figma binds it. The label is 14/20 at both sizes. An icon-only button is square: its width is its height. Contained is lit from above: a lighter top, a highlight on the top edge, a bottom-edge inner shadow (black at 18%, 1px up, 1.2px blur, 0.35px spread) and a hairline border a step darker than the solid. The hairline is the variant's solid moved in lightness, so it has no token of its own and follows the accent and the mode; the highlight and the shadow are light, the same on every fill. ## States }, { label: 'Loading', content: }, ]} > - **Hover and pressed** are mixed from the variant's own colours, not a token each. Button Group is outside the 1.0 component list; it is beta from 0.9.0. ## Variants | `type` | Use for | | --- | --- | | `separate` | The default. Outlined toggles 4px apart: one view, one mode, one period at a time. | | `joined` | A segmented control: one bar, where the options read as one control. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { ButtonGroup } from 'zweihander/button-group' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/button-group.json ``` - Source: [src/components/buttons/ButtonGroup.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/buttons/ButtonGroup.tsx) - Spec: none on uiguideline.com; after [shadcn/ui Button Group](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/button-group) and [Toggle Group](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/toggle-group) - Behaviour: [Base UI Toggle Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toggle-group) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The toggles keep their own anatomy; the container only spaces them (`separate`) or joins them (`joined`). ## Measurements The group adds no size of its own. Each button keeps its tier, so a group of `sm` buttons is `--control-sm` tall. `joined`: the inner corners are square and each toggle after the first overlaps the one before by its 1px border, so two outlined toggles share one line. import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Checkbox } from './Checkbox' import * as CheckboxStories from './Checkbox.stories' # Checkbox Selects an option, or several from a list, to apply when a form is submitted. ## Variants `variant` is the colour of the checked box. Each row: unchecked, checked, indeterminate. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | | The default: lists, forms, tables. The checked box is the foreground colour, so a column of them stays calm. | | | One checkbox that carries the brand: an opt-in, a terms box beside a primary button. | **Indeterminate** is for a parent whose children are partly selected. It is a display state: clicking the parent chooses all or none, never "mixed". ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Checkbox } from 'zweihander/checkbox' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/checkbox.json ``` - Source: [src/components/controls/Checkbox.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Checkbox.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/checkbox](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/checkbox) - Behaviour: [Base UI Checkbox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/checkbox) and [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The label wraps the box, so the whole label is part of the click target. ## Measurements One size. The box is 16px, Atlassian's, inside a 24px hit area, and sits centred on the first line of its label, however many lines the label wraps to. The label starts 8px from the box: Atlassian's 4px gap after the 24px area. The box's corner is the radius step, not the control tier's radius: a box that turned round under `radius="full-rounded"` would read as a radio. The label is regular weight, as Atlassian's checkbox label is; the form label weight is for a field's or a group's label, not an option's. ## Color ## States }, { label: 'Indeterminate', content: }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, { label: 'Error', content: }, ]} > - **Hover** anywhere on the label darkens an unchecked outline to `--color-text`. A checked box mixes 12% of the mark's colour into its fill, as Button does. An error outline stays red. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the box. - **Disabled** dims the box and the label to 50%. - **Read-only** looks enabled but has no hover and an arrow cursor. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`id`, `className`, `aria-label` and `ref` pass through to the box. ### Differences from the spec - **Atlassian's box.** 16px with a 2px corner inside a 24px hit area, and a 12px mark: the kit's own step, since Atlassian draws the mark as part of the box. - **Base UI's and HTML's names:** `defaultChecked` and `onCheckedChange` for the spec's `defaultValue` (a string there, which reads as the submitted value: that is `value`) and `onChange`; native `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` for the `is…` forms. - **`isIndeterminate` keeps its prefix.** Indeterminate is a DOM property, not an HTML attribute, so by the kit's naming rule it takes `is`; Base UI calls it `indeterminate`. - **`autoFocus` is applied on mount by the component.** The box is a focusable ``, which React's own `autoFocus` ignores. - **No `secondary`.** A light fill barely reads as checked, so only `neutral` (the foreground colour) and `primary` ship. ## When to use Use a checkbox for a choice that is submitted with a form: accepting terms, opting in, picking several items from a list. Nothing happens until the form is sent. Write the label so that checked means yes. } doCaption="The label says what checking does: checked means yes." dont={} dontCaption="A negative label makes unchecked a double negative, and readers stop to work it out." /> ## When not to use - **For a setting that applies at once.** Use a [Switch](?path=/docs/components-controls-switch--docs): it acts like a light switch, a checkbox waits for Submit. - **For one choice out of several.** Use a [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group; checkboxes are independent. - **For a toggle in a toolbar.** Use a [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs). ## Accessibility - `role="checkbox"` with `aria-checked`, `mixed` when indeterminate. Space toggles it. - The label wraps the box, so it names it and clicking it toggles the box. Without a visible label, pass `aria-label`: it goes to the box itself. - `helperText` is the box's description; the error state sets `aria-invalid`. - The unchecked outline is `--color-border-bold`, 3:1 on the page on every gray ramp. - A hidden native input carries `name`, `value` and `required` into form submission and validation. - The hit area is 24×24px, 44×44px on coarse pointers, without the box growing.

components-controls-color-picker--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { ColorPicker } from './ColorPicker' import * as ColorPickerStories from './ColorPicker.stories' # Color Picker Chooses a colour: type it in any CSS format, pick a swatch, find it on a saturation and brightness area and a hue strip, or type its channels in Hex, RGB, HSL or HSB. The panel is laid out like Figma's colour picker. ## Variants Two exports. | Export | Use for | | --- | --- | | `ColorPicker` | A form field: the hex in a text field, with a swatch button that opens the panel in a popover. | | `ColorPanel` | The panel on its own, always open: a sidebar, an inspector, a settings page about colour. | `alpha` adds opacity; `defaultFormat` picks which channels the fields show first. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { ColorPicker, ColorPanel } from 'zweihander/color-picker' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/color-picker.json ``` - Source: [src/components/controls/ColorPicker.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/ColorPicker.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/color-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/color-picker) - Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover) and [Slider](https://base-ui.com/react/components/slider) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The panel here is shown open under its field; in a `ColorPicker` the swatch button opens it in a popover 8px under the whole field, aligned to its start, as Select's list and Date Picker's calendar. ## Measurements The field is a Text Input: the same tiers, padding and label. The panel is the same at both field sizes. The panel is 16rem wide, so eight 24px swatches fit in their one row (it does not wrap), and the area is 10rem tall. The format menu and the channels are the kit's sm (32px) Select and field box. ## Color The area, the hue strip and the checkerboard are the colour model itself, so they are fixed colours, not theme tokens. The thumbs are white rings with a dark edge: one of the two is at least 3:1 against whatever colour is under them. Swatches have a faint inner edge, black 10% in light mode and white 10% in dark, as in Figma. That is below the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11 round a white swatch on white, accepted because the hex in the field, not the edge, tells the colour. ## States }, { label: 'Error', content: }, ]} > - **Focus** follows Text Input on the field. In the panel every thumb, swatch and field draws a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside. - **Disabled** dims the field and disables the swatch button. - **Error** is Text Input's. Typed text that is not a colour turns the field to error on its own, with a hint, and keeps the last good value. - **Chosen swatch** has a 2px `--color-background-brand-bold` ring; focused as well, the ring turns `--color-border-focused` and moves 1px further out. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`ColorPanel` takes `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `alpha`, `defaultFormat`, `swatches`, `disabled` and `className`. `parseColor(text)` reads any CSS colour (`rgb(59 130 246)`, `hsl(217 91% 60% / 50%)`, `oklch(...)`, `rebeccapurple`) to the same hex, or `null`; the browser parses it, so outside one only hex is read. `normalizeHex(text)` turns `#abc`, `ABC` or `#AABBCC` into `#aabbcc`, keeps an alpha byte (`#3b82f680`, or `#abc8` as `#aabbcc88`) unless it is `ff`, and turns anything else into `null`. ### Design notes - **Hex in, hex out.** The value is lowercase `#rrggbb`, with an alpha byte only while opacity is under 100%. Typed text is read on Enter or blur: hex of 3, 4, 6 or 8 digits with or without `#`, or any CSS colour. It is shown back as hex. - **Formats are a view, not a value.** RGB, HSL and HSB only change the fields; the value stays hex. Channel fields commit on Enter or blur, and up and down step by 1 (Shift by 10), as in a design tool. - **The hue is remembered.** The picker keeps hue, saturation and brightness, so dragging to black and back leaves the hue strip where it was instead of jumping to red. - **Not in this version:** Figma's library picker ("On this page"), gradients and an eyedropper. ## When to use Use a colour picker when any colour is a valid answer: a brand colour, a chart series, a label someone defines. When there is a palette to follow, offer it as named swatches. } doCaption="The colours people should use, as named swatches: one click, and a screen reader says “Blue”, not a hex." dont={} dontCaption="A palette to follow but no swatches: people match it by eye and land a few steps off." /> ## When not to use - **For a few fixed colours.** When only a set of colours is allowed (tag colours, a theme accent), use a [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group of swatches or a Select: the picker lets anyone type any colour. - **To show a colour.** Use a swatch and its hex as text. ## Accessibility - The field is a text input named by its label. The component is `RadioGroup`. ## Variants `variant` is the colour of the selected radio; `orientation` lays the options out in a column or a row. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `neutral` | The default: forms and settings. The selected radio is the foreground colour. | | `primary` | A choice that carries the brand: a plan picker beside a primary button. | | Orientation | Use for | | --- | --- | | `vertical` | The default. Options with helper text, or labels longer than a word or two. | | `horizontal` | Two to four short labels: sizes, yes or no. The row wraps when narrow. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { RadioGroup } from 'zweihander/radio' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/radio.json ``` - Source: [src/components/controls/Radio.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Radio.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/radio](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/radio) - Behaviour: [Base UI Radio Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/radio), [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field) and [Fieldset](https://base-ui.com/react/components/fieldset) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Each option's label wraps its radio, so the whole label is part of the click target. ## Measurements One size. The circle is 16px, Atlassian's, inside a 24px hit area, and sits centred on the first line of its label, however many lines the label wraps to. The label starts 8px from the circle: Atlassian's 4px gap after the 24px area. Stacked options are 4px apart, one every 24px, so their hit areas meet without overlapping. The legend is the body size at Atlassian's form label weight, 653 (its Legend and Label share it). An option's own label is regular weight, as Atlassian's radio and checkbox labels are. ## Color An option's own helper describes the option, so it stays muted when the group is in error or success; only the group message takes that colour. ## States }, { label: 'Error', content: }, ]} > - **Hover** anywhere on an option's label darkens an unselected ring to `--color-text`. The selected radio mixes 12% of the dot's colour into its fill, as Button does. An error ring stays red. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the circle. - **Disabled** dims the radio and its label to 50%, for the whole group or one option. - **Read-only** looks enabled but has no hover and an arrow cursor. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}

Following the kit's "flat props" convention, the radios are `options` rather than child components. - **`checked` and `autoFocus` per radio are not props.** The group's `value` says which is checked. - Base UI's `onValueChange` and native `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` names, as on Checkbox. - **No `secondary`.** A light fill barely reads as selected, so only `neutral` (the foreground colour) and `primary` ship, as on Checkbox. ## When to use Use radios to choose one option from a short list, when seeing every option at once helps the choice: a plan, a delivery method, a size. Up to about six options. Select the usual choice by default when there is one. } doCaption="A few options, all in view, the usual one already selected." dont={} dontCaption="Ten radios are a wall to scan. ` with a ``, exposed as a `radiogroup` named by the legend. - **One tab stop for the group.** Tab enters at the selected radio (or the first), arrow keys move and select, Tab leaves. Whole stars only. | | | Showing: an average beside a product. Fractions draw as a star filled part-way. | `getValueText` changes what each score is called, for a scale that is not stars: ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Rating } from 'zweihander/rating' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/rating.json ``` - Source: [src/components/controls/Rating.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Rating.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/rating](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/rating) - Behaviour: native radio buttons; no Base UI part covers it - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Each star is a label over an invisible native radio, so arrows, Tab and form submission are the browser's own. It is 2.1:1 on white, below the 3:1 a meaningful graphic needs, so colour is not what carries the score: the group or image is named "3 out of 5 stars". `className` passes through to the group. ## When to use Use a rating to ask for, or show, a quick score on a short scale: a review, a difficulty, how useful something was. Keep the scale short: five stars is the convention readers already know. } doCaption="Five stars: few enough to hit and to tell apart at a glance." dont={} dontCaption="Ten stars are small targets, and 7 looks much like 8. Use a Slider or a Number Input for a fine scale." /> ## When not to use - **For a precise number.** Use a [Slider](?path=/docs/components-controls-slider--docs) or a Number Input. - **For a choice between named options.** Use a [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group, so the options say what they mean. - **To show progress.** Use a Progress Bar. ## Accessibility - Interactive: a `
` named by its legend (or `aria-label`), with one radio per star named "1 out of 5 stars" and so on (change the words with `getValueText`). Arrows move the choice; Tab moves into and out of the group. - Read-only: `role="img"` named with the value, "4.5 out of 5 stars". - Hover previews the score; focus shows the 2px ring round the star. - Filled and empty stars share one shape and differ by colour only, so the score is always in the name: the group's checked radio, or the image's label. - Stars grow a 44px target on coarse pointers.

Off is the same in every variant. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | | The default: most settings. | | | Neutral black or white, where the brand colour would clash or already means something else. | | | A setting that is risky to leave on: public sharing, deleting old data automatically. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Switch } from 'zweihander/switch' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/switch.json ``` - Source: [src/components/controls/Switch.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Switch.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/switch](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/switch) - Behaviour: [Base UI Switch](https://base-ui.com/react/components/switch) and [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The label wraps the track, so the whole label is part of the click target. ## Measurements Two tracks, Atlassian's: 32×16px (`md`, the default) and 40×20px (`lg`). Each is twice as wide as it is tall, so the thumb travels one track height. The thumb sits 2px inside the track at both sizes. `size="sm"` is deprecated. It draws the `md` track, warns once in development, and will be removed in the next release: drop the prop. `md` (the default, written out or not) and `lg` are silent. ## Color Off is a `--color-border-bold` track (3:1 on the page, so the control is visible at all) with a page-coloured thumb. On takes the variant's solid, and the thumb its label colour, measured at 4.5:1 against it. ## States }, { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, { label: 'Error', content: }, ]} > - **Hover** changes only the cursor: the track has no lighter or darker step to move to without losing its 3:1. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the track. - **Disabled** dims the track and the label to 50%. - **Error** draws a 2px `--color-text-danger` ring outside the track, as Figma's outside stroke. Atlassian's toggle draws no visible label of its own (its `label` is hidden text for a screen reader); a form there puts a separate form Label next to it. - **Base UI's names:** `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange` for the spec's `defaultValue` and `onChange`; native `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` for `isDisabled`, `isRequired`, `isReadOnly`. - **`helperText` is added.** `validationState="error"` needs somewhere to say what is wrong; colour alone is not a message. ## When to use Use a switch for a setting that takes effect the moment it is flipped, like a light switch: dark mode, notifications, auto-save. } doCaption="The setting applies as soon as the switch moves." dont={} dontCaption="A switch that waits for Save looks done when it is not. Use a checkbox in a form." /> ## When not to use - **For a choice submitted with a form.** Use a [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs). - **For more than two options.** Use a [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group or a Select. - **For a toggle in a toolbar** (Bold, a filter). import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Calendar } from './Calendar' import * as CalendarStories from './Calendar.stories' # Calendar A month grid to pick one day from, or to show one: a booking page, the inside of a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs). ## Variants Calendar has one look and one size. What changes is what it shows. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | One day (`value`) | Picking or showing a single day: a delivery date, a booking. | | A span (`range`) | Showing a stay or a report period. Clicks still report one day; Date Range Picker decides the span. | | Limits (`min`, `max`) | Booking windows: nothing before tomorrow, nothing after the season ends. | | Ruled-out days (`isDateDisabled`) | Weekends, holidays, days already booked. | | Locale (`locale`, `weekStartsOn`) | Month and weekday names in the reader's language, and their first day of the week. | The locale decides the week: `vi-VN` and `en-GB` start on Monday, `en-US` on Sunday, read from `Intl.Locale` where the browser knows it (Monday otherwise). The grid is always Gregorian, so a locale whose own calendar is not (Persian) still gets Gregorian days, in its own digits. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Calendar } from 'zweihander/calendar' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/calendar.json ``` - Source: [src/components/data-display/Calendar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Calendar.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/calendar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/calendar) - Behaviour: a plain element, using `Intl` for names and the week's first day: no date library - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The grid always has six rows. Months span four to six weeks; a fixed height keeps a popover or a page from jumping as you page through them. Two more looks sit on the days: **today**, an orange fill with the control's corners, as a selected day has; and with `range`, the **band**, as tall as a day, one unbroken strip behind the days from one end to the other. Under the two ends it covers only the half that faces the range, so each end keeps its own corners on the outside. The band rounds off where a week or the month starts or ends. Days of the months either side are never banded, so two months side by side never draw the same day twice. ## Measurements Calendar has one size, after `@atlaskit/calendar`. Days are 40px wide and 32px tall and touch: the whole cell is the day's target, and a range's band runs unbroken from cell to cell. The weekday row is 32px tall, 8px round a 16px line of bold 12px. The header keeps 8px at each end and sits 12px above the grid; its arrows are 24px round a 12px chevron. In a Date Picker the panel adds 16px round all of it. The header is one row: previous month at the start, the month and year centred, in the 14px heading size, and next month at the end. There are no year buttons; Shift+Page Up and Shift+Page Down page by year. The kit keeps its own looks for today and the selected day. Figures are tabular, so the columns of dates line up. On touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) days grow to 44px square, the touch target: they touch, so a larger invisible area would lie over the next day. The previous and next buttons stay 24px and grow an invisible 44px area instead. The header makes room for them: it pads 10px (half of 44px less 24px) and the month keeps 10px clear at each side, so the areas lie over neither the month nor the calendar's edge. ## Color One table per kind of day. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. - **Day** has no fill at rest. - **Today's figure** is `--color-text-accent-orange-contrast`, semibold: near-black on `--color-background-accent-orange-bolder`, 4.9:1 in both modes. White would be 3.4:1 in light, under the 4.5:1 a 14px figure needs. A selected today shows as selected. - **Days between** the ends of a range are `--color-text`, regular weight. - **Outside days** are `--color-text-subtlest` mixed 50% with transparent, about 2:1. No token is lighter, and WCAG allows it for decoration: they are hidden from assistive tech and cannot be picked. - **Unavailable days** are struck through as well as faded, so they do not rely on colour. ## States }, { label: 'Today', content: }, ]} /> }]} /> Each example forces the state on every day at once; on screen it is the one under the pointer or the keyboard. - **Hover** fills a day, or the previous and next buttons, with `--color-background-neutral` behind `--color-text`. The selected day and today keep their own colours; unavailable and outside days do not react. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the day. The days touch, so the focused day is lifted above its neighbours and the ring is drawn whole over their edges. - **Pressed** has no look of its own: the click selects the day, and the selected look follows. - **Disabled** is per day: before `min`, after `max`, or ruled out by `isDateDisabled`. The previous and next buttons disable in the month of `min` or `max`, at 50% opacity. - **Selected** is the brand fill, with the control's corners; **today** is the orange fill, with the same corners. With `range`, both ends are selected and the days between are banded. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Also exported, for working with the same plain dates: `isSameDay`, `addDays`, `addMonths`, `startOfDay`, `firstDayOfWeek` and the `DateRange` type. Every date is local midnight; times are ignored. ### Differences from the spec The header follows `@atlaskit/calendar` in the size of its buttons and the centred month and year, without its year buttons: Shift+Page Up and Shift+Page Down page by year. - **The buttons disable at `min` and `max`.** Atlassian's stay enabled and page into months with nothing to pick. - **Fixed button names.** "Previous month" and "Next month", in English like the kit's other built-in labels. Atlassian takes them as props and adds the month they lead to ("Previous month, August 2026"). - **The month is not a heading.** Atlassian's is one, with a level prop; a calendar can sit anywhere in a page's outline, so here it is a plain live region, and the grid is named with the same text. - **Always a live region.** Atlassian turns `aria-live` on after the first press of a header button; here it is there from the start, which announces nothing until the month changes. - **Semibold is 600**, as the kit's other headings; Atlassian's heading weight is 653. ## When to use Use a Calendar where the day is picked by looking at the month: a booking page, a delivery slot, a few weeks either side of today. Rule out the days that cannot be picked with `min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled`, rather than refusing the choice after it is made. } doCaption="A date close to now, where seeing the week matters: unavailable days are struck through before anyone picks them." dont={} dontCaption="A date of birth is decades away: paging back a month, or even a year, at a time is slow. Type it in a Date Picker." /> Month steps keep the day where they can: 31 January plus a month is 28 February, not 3 March. ## When not to use - **For a date far from today**, or one people know by heart, like a date of birth. Use a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs): it takes the date typed, and opens this calendar when wanted. - **For a span inside a form.** Use a [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs): it owns the two clicks that make a span and shows it here. - **For a schedule of events.** A day here holds a number, not content. List the events in a [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs). ## Accessibility - A `role="grid"` named by the month and year ("September 2026"), with column headers that carry the full weekday name in `abbr`. - Each day is a button named by its full date ("Friday 18 September 2026"). The selected cell has `aria-selected`, and with `range` every cell from one end to the other does. Today has `aria-current="date"`. - One tab stop: the selected day, or today when nothing is selected. - Arrow keys move a day or a week, Home and End go to the week's ends, Page Up and Page Down move a month, and Shift+Page Up and Shift+Page Down a year. Enter or Space selects. Moving past the month shows the next one. - Right to left, the arrows follow the screen (ArrowLeft is the next day) and the previous and next chevrons are mirrored. - The month and year are a polite live region, so paging is announced, by a month or by a year. - The header's buttons are ordinary buttons in the tab order, before the grid: "Previous month", then after the month "Next month". - Both are disabled at the limits: previous in the month of `min`, next in the month of `max`. - Unavailable days stay focusable with `aria-disabled`, so they are found and announced as unavailable rather than skipped. Enter on one does nothing. - Days of the months either side are not buttons and are hidden from assistive tech. - Today's figure should measure at least 4.5:1 on its fill, in both modes, on its own and inside a range. The `Today` story measures it.

With `onClick` the whole card is one button; with `render={}` it is a link. `isRounded={false}` gives square corners. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Card } from 'zweihander/card' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/card.json ``` - Source: [src/components/data-display/Card.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Card.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/card](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/card) - Composition: [Base UI useRender](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/use-render) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The card is only the container. That keeps the choice yours to store, per user or per view. With a resizable Table, pass `onReset` to put the widths back too: ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { ColumnChooser } from 'zweihander/column-chooser' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/column-chooser.json ``` - Source: [src/components/data-display/ColumnChooser.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/ColumnChooser.tsx) - Spec: none on uiguideline.com; built from the Application UI catalogue, whose source for widths is shadcn's Resizable. Widths are Table's `isResizable` instead, a handle in each header rather than resizable panels - Behaviour: the kit's [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs), [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs) and [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs); the popup is styled as a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs) list's shell and options - Figma: the Column Chooser component in the library ## Anatomy The open popovers on this tab and the next are pictures: real choosers rendered in place with `container` and inert, the popup laid out under the button where it opens. ## Measurements The button is a medium Button. The popup is a list's shell, as Select's, with Popover's border, `--radius-lg` corner and `--shadow-overlay`: 240px wide (or the screen's width, if narrower), 8px above and below the rows and none at the sides, so a row's hover fill runs edge to edge. Each column is an option's row, 32px, and the whole row is the click target: it is the checkbox's label, stretched. Reset columns is one more row, its text in line with the column names. Rows grow to 44px on touch screens. ## Color The button is an outlined secondary Button and the popup's surface is Popover's `--color-surface-overlay`; see those pages for their tokens. ## States The chooser is open or closed. The button keeps Button's states; each box keeps Checkbox's, and a locked column shows Checkbox's disabled look. A row and Reset take `--color-background-neutral` on hover; Reset's focus ring is drawn inside it: - **Locked**: the row header column, and the last column left, are ticked and disabled: a table needs a name per row and at least one column. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
### Differences from the spec There is no uiguideline spec. The catalogue's anatomy lists drag to reorder as optional; it is left out until a table needs it, because it needs a keyboard way to move as well. The popup is a dialog with no visible title, named by `label`: it holds checkboxes and a button, which a `listbox` cannot. ## When to use Use a Column Chooser on a table with more columns than most people need at once, typically six or more, where different people read different ones. } doCaption="A few optional columns beside a locked name column." dont={} dontCaption="A chooser for two columns: one is locked, so there is nothing to choose." /> ## When not to use - **To switch between whole layouts** (a summary and a detailed set): use saved views, so one choice changes several columns at once. - **To filter rows.** Hiding a column does not hide rows; use filters in the table's toolbar. - **For a table that fits.** If every column fits on the screens it is used on, leave them all shown. ## Accessibility - The button reports `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`. The popup is a `role="dialog"` named by the label, "Columns", through `aria-label`: it shows no title. - Opening moves focus into the dialog; Escape closes it and returns focus to the button. - Each column is a checkbox named by its header, in table order; Space toggles it, and so does a click anywhere on its row. The shown keys are reported in column order, the row header always among them. - The row header column's checkbox, and the last checked one, are `aria-disabled`: ticked and unchangeable. - Reset is a button named "Reset columns" that brings back the default columns, after a `role="separator"`.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as TableStories from './Table.stories' # Table Rows of records with the same fields, to scan and compare: projects, invoices, members. Columns can sort, rows can be selected, expanded and acted on, and a total row can sum them up. ## Variants Table has one size: 8px round each cell, so a row of text is 36px, and a row that holds a button or a field grows to fit it. Any table takes any of these together: a selectable table can also expand its rows and keep its header in view. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `isSelectable` | Acting on several rows at once: archive, export, assign. | | `expandedContent` | Details that belong to one row but do not fit in a column: a description, a timeline, line items. | | `hasStickyHeader` | Long tables that scroll inside a fixed height, so the column names stay in view. | | `rowActions` | Actions on one record (edit, duplicate, archive) that do not earn a column: a menu at the row's end. | | `footer` on a column | A total row under the rows: sums, counts, averages. | | `isResizable` | Tables whose columns hold text of unknown length (names, notes, emails), so people can widen what they read. | | `emptyState` | Saying why there are no rows, and what to do: clear a search, add the first one. | Rows with details open under themselves. Expansion is independent of selection and survives sorting: A menu at the end of each row. A row with nothing to do gets no button: A total row under the rows, which sorting leaves at the bottom. The table does not add anything up: you pass each column's `footer`, so you decide whether it totals this page or every row. A handle on each header's end edge resizes its column, by dragging or by the arrow keys. The table is then laid out by its header widths: give the columns a starting `width`, and keep `columnWidths` if they should last. Pair it with a [Column Chooser](?path=/docs/components-data-display-column-chooser--docs) to hide columns as well. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Table, type TableColumn } from 'zweihander/table' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/table.json ``` - Source: [src/components/data-display/Table.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Table.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/table](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/table) - Behaviour: a native ``; selection uses the kit's [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs), expansion its [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs), row actions its [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The table sits in a container that scrolls sideways on a narrow screen rather than squeezing the columns. The selection column comes first, then the expand column; the actions column comes last. A row whose `expandedContent` or `rowActions` returns nothing leaves that cell empty. The total row is a ``, so it stays at the bottom whatever the sort. ## Measurements A row has no height of its own: it is as tall as what its cells hold. | What the row holds | Row height | | --- | --- | | One line of text (20px), or a Tag | 36px | | A checkbox, an expand button or an actions button (24px) | 36px | | A 24px button | 40px | | A 32px button or field | 48px | | Header (one 16px line) | 32px | A body row is exactly that tall: there is no divider under it. The header and the total row add their 1px rule, and a table that has rows adds one more under its last row. The checkbox, expand and actions columns take 2px less block padding than the other cells, so their 24px buttons do not make a row of text taller. The handle line is 1px at rest; no token covers a hairline. Its strip is 16px wide (44px on touch screens), at the header's end, over the header's own padding. The last column's handle sits on the table's edge and shows its line only on hover and drag. A column is 48px to 1200px wide; the arrow keys move it 16px at a time. Rows have no divider between them: the hover tint and the selection fill tell them apart. The header ends on a 1px rule and its labels are semibold; the total row sits under the same rule, so the sum reads as a sum. A table that has rows closes on that rule too, as Atlassian's dynamic table: under the last row, an open row's content or the total row, whichever comes last. It is the table's own border, so under a sticky header it scrolls with the rows, and whatever a page puts under the table (a Pagination, a footer) keeps its own gap below the rule. An empty table has no closing rule: the header's is the only one over the empty state. The sort button pulls itself out by its own padding, so its label lines up with the cells below and its hover fill adds nothing to the header's height. **Every cell is padded 8px all round**, the first and last of a row included: the first column's text, the caption and an open row's content all start 8px in from the table's left edge, and an end-aligned last column ends 8px short of its right edge. The control columns are their control with 8px either side: 32px for the 16px checkbox, 40px for the 24px expand and actions buttons. Focus rings in the control columns are drawn inside the control, because the cell has no room for an outset ring. Figures are tabular, so numbers line up column-wide. ## Color Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. - The header has no fill. With `hasStickyHeader` it takes the container's own `--color-surface-raised`, only so the rows scroll under it. - Rows are not striped, and have no divider: hover and selection tint the row under the pointer or the checkbox, from edge to edge. - The sort icon of a column that is not sorted is `--color-text-subtlest`; the sorted column's is the brand colour. - **Two selected rows next to each other** read as one filled block; each row's checkbox says which are in it. - **An open row and its content read as one block**: the content row shares its row's hover and selected tint, and its 16px block-end padding sets the pair apart from the next row. ## States }, { label: 'Selected', content: }, ]} /> }]} /> Each example forces the state on every row and button at once; on screen it is the one under the pointer or the keyboard. - **Hover** tints the row with `--color-background-neutral`, and the sort button too. The content row of an open row takes no hover of its own, only its row's. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, drawn 2px inside the sort button. The checkboxes and the expand button keep their own focus rings. - **Pressed** has no look of its own: the click sorts, selects or opens, and that state's look follows. - **Resize handle**: hover and drag thicken its line to 2px `--color-background-brand-bold`; focus draws the `--color-border-focused` outline inside the handle. - **Disabled**: Table has none. A row that cannot be acted on is a row without the control. - **Sorted** shows the column's icon at full colour, pointing up or down. - **Selected** tints the row with `--color-background-brand-subtlest`. - **Expanded** turns the chevron to point down and opens the content row under it. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`TableColumn` describes one column: - `key`: unique; also the row field shown when there is no `cell`. - `header`: the column's label. - `cell`: renders the cell; defaults to `row[key]`. - `sortable`: adds a sort button to the header. It sorts by `sortValue`, or by `row[key]`. - `align`: `start`, `center` or `end`. `end` for numbers and dates, so the digits line up. - `width`: any CSS width, e.g. `8rem` or `20%`. - `isRowHeader`: makes the column's cells `
`, the name a row is known by. Usually the first column. - `footer`: this column's cell in the total row, e.g. a sum. Any column with one adds the row; put the label ("Total") on the row header column. Hidden while there are no rows. `TableSort` is `{ key, direction }`, with direction `ascending` or `descending`. `size` and `density` are deprecated. Table has one size, as Atlassian's does: `size="sm"` (and `density="sm"`) renders the same table as `md`. Both are still accepted for one release; drop them. The kit's rule for a deprecated prop: it warns in the development console when it is passed a value that is not its documented default, and a renamed prop warns whenever it is used. So `size="sm"` and any `density` warn, and `size="md"`, the default written out, is silent. With `sort` controlled, the table leaves the order to you. `sortRows(rows, columns, sort)` returns the rows in the order the table would sort them, so you can sort every row before slicing out a page. ### Differences from the spec Cell sizing follows the Figma library: Atlassian's dynamic table with 8px round every cell. - **No row height, and one size.** A cell has 8px padding all round and the row is as tall as its content; rows were a fixed 48px and 40px before, picked by `density` and then `size`, which are deprecated. - **No row dividers.** Only the 1px rule under the header and the one that closes a table with rows, as Atlassian draws them; rows are told apart by the hover tint and the selection fill. - **The total row has a 1px rule above it.** Atlassian's table has no total row; the rule is the header's, turned over. The table's closing rule then sits under the total row. - **No header fill, and padded edges.** The header is its labels over the rule, as Atlassian's dynamic table. Unlike Atlassian's, the first and last cells keep their 8px at the table's edge. The hover and selection tints run edge to edge. - **The caption** sits 24px from the top and 8px above the table, 8px in from the edge where the cells' text starts. Its type stays the cells' size, semibold; Atlassian's is a 20px heading. ## When to use Use a Table for records that share their fields, when people compare them or look one up: projects, invoices, members. Align numbers and dates to the end, and mark the column a row is known by with `isRowHeader`. } doCaption="Numbers and dates aligned to the end, in tabular figures: the digits line up column-wide." dont={} dontCaption="Aligned to the start, 9 sits under the 1 of 1,203, and the column cannot be compared at a glance." /> } doCaption="A row header names each row, so its checkbox reads “Select Atlas”." dont={} dontCaption="Without one, every checkbox is “Select row 1”, “Select row 2”: a screen reader user cannot tell what they select." /> **Sort cycles ascending, descending, off.** The third click returns to the original order, which is often the one that meant something. Uncontrolled, the table sorts a copy: dates as dates, numbers as numbers, text by locale with "file 2" before "file 10". Empty values sort last both ways. With server-side sorting, pass `sort` and `onSortChange` and hand back the rows already sorted: **Paging is not built in.** Put a [Pagination](?path=/docs/components-navigation-pagination--docs) under the table and pass it one page of `rows`. With `getRowId`, selection keeps working across pages: "Select all" adds or removes this page's rows only. Pass `expandedIds` to open rows from outside the table: ## When not to use - **For records that do not share fields**, or that are read one at a time, like products in a shop. Use [Cards](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs). - **For layout.** A table announces rows and columns to a screen reader; use CSS grid to place things side by side. - **For a spreadsheet**, where arrow keys move between cells and cells are edited in place. Table is a plain table, not an ARIA grid; the kit has no data grid yet. ## Accessibility - A real `` named by its `` with one cell per column, so each total is announced under its column; the label column is its row header.
`, with `
` headers and a `` for the row header column: screen readers announce the column and the row for every cell. - Sortable headers carry `aria-sort` (`ascending`, `descending` or `none`); the sort control is a button inside the header. - Row checkboxes are named after the row header ("Select Atlas"), or "Select row 1" without one, counted from `rows` so a sort does not rename them. The header checkbox is "Select all rows" and reports `mixed` when some are selected. A selected row has `aria-selected`. - Each expand button is named after the row header ("Expand Atlas"), reports `aria-expanded`, and while open points at the content cell with `aria-controls`. Enter and Space toggle it. The name stays the same open or closed; `aria-expanded` carries the state. - A row with nothing to expand has no button. - The expand column's header is "Details", visually hidden, so the column is announced like the others. - The content cell spans every column, so it is read as one cell under its row. - Each row actions button is named after the row header ("Actions for Atlas") and reports `aria-haspopup="menu"`. Enter opens the menu, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the button. A row with no items has no button. - The actions column's header is "Actions", visually hidden. - When the table is wider than its box and nothing in it takes focus, the scroll box becomes a tab stop with a focus ring: `role="region"` named by the caption, which the browser scrolls with the arrow keys. A table that fits, or whose cells hold a control (a sort button, a checkbox), gets no extra tab stop. - With `isResizable`, each column header holds a focusable `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation="vertical"`, named "Resize" and the header ("Resize Owner"), or the column's `key` when the header is not plain text. Its `aria-valuenow` is the column's width in px, between `aria-valuemin` 48 and `aria-valuemax` 1200. - Arrow Right widens the column 16px and Arrow Left narrows it (mirrored in right-to-left); Home sets the narrowest width and End the widest. ) # Combobox A field you type into to filter a list of options, then choose one. ## Variants Two sizes, and the field's validation states. Typing filters the list and marks the match; the chosen option carries a check. | Size | Use for | | --- | --- | | `md` | Forms and settings: the default. | | `sm` | Dense places: a toolbar filter, a table row. As tall as a default Button. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Combobox } from 'zweihander/combobox' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/combobox.json ``` - Source: [src/components/inputs/Combobox.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Combobox.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/combobox](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/combobox) - Behaviour: [Base UI Combobox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The options list opens under the field, at least as wide as it: - **Option**: the label, with the typed text marked by weight and underline. Options are inset by the field's padding, so their text starts where the input's does. - **Check**: before the chosen option's label, in a column kept for every option so labels never shift. - **Message**: "No matches" (`emptyText`) when nothing matches, "Loading…" while `isLoading`. ## Measurements A field is one step taller than a Button, after Atlassian Design: `sm` is 32px and `md` is 40px (Foundations / Sizing). The sizes share the rest: 10px of padding at each end, the 16px icons, 12px apart, the field radius, which never becomes a pill, and body type. The clear button is the bare 16px icon; the open button is a 24px target round its icon, which ends 10px inside the edge. The text stops 12px short of the first icon. The field is 20rem wide unless `isFullWidth`; the list is at least as wide as the field, 4px under it, and scrolls after 20rem (about ten options). ## Color The field's edge is a light hairline, about 1.5:1, as in the Claude apps: an approved exception to WCAG 1.4.11. The label, placeholder and focus ring still mark the field. The matched text keeps the option's own colour, so it holds full contrast on the highlighted row. ## States }, { label: 'Error', content: }, { label: 'Read-only', content: }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, { label: 'Loading', content: }, ]} > - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the field, drawn while the input has focus, by pointer too: that is where typing goes. In the error state the ring is `--color-text-danger`. The clear and open buttons draw their own ring when tabbed to, so the field never shows two. - **Hover** changes nothing on the field; the clear and open buttons darken from `--color-text-subtlest` to `--color-text`. - **Error** turns the edge and the helper `--color-text-danger` together; the words are the message, the colour only points at it. - **Read-only** fills the field with `--color-background-input`; there is no clear button. - **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity. - **Loading** adds a spinner before the buttons and says "Loading…" in the list. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}

Typing a few letters is faster than scrolling. It chooses from the list only; free text that is not an option is not a value. } doCaption="A long list people know an entry of: type a few letters, pick it." dont={} dontCaption="Three options hidden behind typing. A Select or a radio group shows them all." /> ## When not to use - **For a handful of options.** Under about seven, use a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs), or a [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group when they should all be visible. - **For free text.** If any answer is valid, use a [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs); to filter a page, use [Search](?path=/docs/components-inputs-search--docs). - **For several values.** It holds one; a multi-select is not built yet. ## Accessibility - The input has `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"` and `aria-expanded`; the list is a `listbox` named by the field's label (or `aria-label` when there is no visible label), as the input is. - **Keyboard:** typing opens and filters; the first match is highlighted so Enter picks it; Up and Down move; Escape closes, then clears. - The match is marked by weight and underline, not colour, so it keeps the option's full contrast on the highlighted row. - The open button is named "Show options" and is out of the tab order (the input already opens the list); the clear button is "Clear selection". - `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid`, and the helper text is the input's description. - Loading and empty states are announced from the list. - After an option is picked with the pointer, the input loses focus and the field returns to rest (no caret, no ring). A keyboard pick keeps focus in the input, so keyboard and screen reader users are not dropped to the page. - Options are 32px tall; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) they grow to 44px, and the clear and open buttons get a 44×44px hit area.
