The typed order follows `locale`: day first in `en-GB` and `vi-VN`, month first in `en-US`. The form always gets `yyyy-mm-dd`. | Locale | Typed as | | --- | --- | | `en-GB`, `vi-VN` | `dd/mm/yyyy` | | `en-US` | `mm/dd/yyyy` | `min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled` limit what can be picked or typed: For a span of days, see [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs). ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { DatePicker } from 'zweihander/date-picker' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/date-picker.json ``` - Source: [src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/date-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/date-picker) - Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover), and the kit's [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The calendar opens in a popover 8px under the field, aligned to its start: a [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs) in a panel. Its days, header and paging buttons are specified there. ## Measurements The field is the kit's field: `sm` is 32px and `md` is 40px, one step taller than a Button, with the same 10px padding, icon and type in both. The calendar button is a 16px icon in a 24px target, pulled into the padding so the icon ends 10px inside the edge, 8px after the date. The field is 20rem wide unless `isFullWidth`. The popover never grows wider than the screen less 16px a side. ## Color The field's edge is a light hairline, about 1.5:1: an approved exception to WCAG 1.4.11, as on every kit field. The calendar's own colours are on its page. ## States }, { label: 'Filled' }, { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' }, { label: 'Error', content: , }, { label: 'Read-only', content: }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, ]} > - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the field, drawn while the input has focus, by pointer too. In the error state the ring is `--color-text-danger`. The calendar button draws its own ring when tabbed to. - **Error** turns the edge and the helper `--color-text-danger`. It is also shown on its own while the typed text is not a date, or is outside `min` and `max`: the helper then gives the expected pattern. - **Hover** changes nothing on the field; the calendar icon darkens from `--color-text-subtlest` to `--color-text`. - **Read-only** fills the box with `--color-background-input`, as every Zweihänder field does. The input stays focusable and copyable and its value is submitted; the calendar icon stays but is not a button, so the calendar never opens. Say why in `helperText`. - **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity; the calendar button is disabled with it. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
### Design notes - **Typing is first-class.** Many people type a known date faster than they can page to it. Any separator works (`3.10.26`, `3/10/2026`); the field reformats on blur or Enter. - **An impossible date is kept, not guessed.** `31/02/2026` stays as typed, the field turns to its error state and the helper shows the expected pattern; nothing is reported until it is a real date. - **A click in the input opens the calendar, and keeps focus there.** Typing carries on with the month in view; the calendar button and Alt+Down move focus into the calendar instead. - **The form gets ISO.** Whatever the display order, `name` submits `yyyy-mm-dd`, so the server never has to guess the locale. ### Differences from the spec - **`onValueChange`, not `onChange`**, with a `Date` or `null`, as the kit's other value fields. ## When to use Use a Date Picker for one date: a start date, a due date, a booking. Let people type it when they know it, and pick it when they want to see the week around it. Set `min`, `max` or `isDateDisabled` so a date that cannot be used cannot be chosen, rather than refusing it after submit. } doCaption="The empty field shows the pattern to type, in the locale's order." dont={} dontCaption="An example date as the placeholder reads as a value already filled in." /> ## When not to use - **For a span of days.** Use a [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs): one field, both ends, never back to front. - **To show a month on the page.** Use a [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs) inline. - **For a time of day.** The picker holds a date only. ## Accessibility - The input is a labelled text box with `inputmode="numeric"` for a number keypad; while the text is not a valid date it has `aria-invalid` and the helper explains the format. Without a visible label, pass `aria-label` to name the input. - The calendar button is named "Choose date", with the current date when there is one. Alt+Down in the input opens it too. - `readOnly` puts `readonly` on the input: screen readers announce it, it stays in the tab order, and there is no calendar button; a click or Alt+Down opens nothing. - The calendar opens as a dialog named "Choose date" with focus on the selected day; Escape closes it without a change. - **After a pick the field goes back to rest.** Picked with the pointer, focus leaves the field (no caret, no ring), as in Combobox. Picked with the keyboard, focus returns to where it came from (the button, or the input), so keyboard and screen reader users are not dropped to the page. - The field and calendar's own labels ("Choose date", "Previous month") are in English, like the rest of the kit's built-in labels. - On touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) the calendar button gets a 44×44px hit area without the field growing.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { DateRangePicker } from './DatePicker' import * as DateRangePickerStories from './DateRangePicker.stories' # Date Range Picker A field for a span of days: a report period, a booking. Typed like [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs), or picked from two months side by side. ## Variants Two sizes, `sm` and `md`, and the field's validation states, as on Date Picker. With `presets`, whole periods sit beside the calendars. | Option | Use for | | --- | --- | | No presets | Ranges that rarely line up with a calendar period: a booking, a leave request. | | `presets` | Reports and filters, where people mostly want "Last month" or "This year". | ## Resources Shipped in the same file as Date Picker, which it shares its field and popover with. From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { DateRangePicker } from 'zweihander/date-picker' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/date-picker.json ``` - Source: [src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/date-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/date-picker) - Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover), and the kit's [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The popover holds: - **Presets**, with `presets`: whole periods, Today to Last year, in a column beside the calendars, or a row above them on a narrow screen. - **Calendars**: two months that page on their own, opening on the range's first and last months (this month and the next when empty). The left one always stays before the right: paging one past the other pushes the other along. One month on a screen narrower than 50rem. ## Measurements The field is Date Picker's: `sm` is 32px and `md` is 40px, with the same padding, icon and type in both. Presets are 2px apart and at least 7rem wide in the column. The field is 20rem wide unless `isFullWidth`; a range is longer than one date, so give it room or `isFullWidth`. ## Color The days and the band between the range's ends are the [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs)'s colours. ## States }, { label: 'Filled' }, { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' }, { label: 'Error', content: , }, { label: 'Read-only', content: , }, { label: 'Disabled', content: , }, ]} > The field's states are Date Picker's: a `--color-border-focused` outline while the input has focus, `--color-text-danger` in error (also while the typed text is not a range), `--color-background-input` and no calendar button when read-only, 50% opacity when disabled. A preset matching the picked range stays in its pressed look. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
### Design notes - **Either way round.** The first click starts the range, the second ends it; a second click before the first swaps them. So does typing the later date first. - **Presets are whole periods.** "This month" is the 1st to the last day, not the 1st to today, so a preset reads the same all month. - **No Cancel or Apply.** A range applies, and the popover closes, once both ends are in; Escape before the second click leaves the value as it was. - **No hover preview.** The band shows once both ends are in; add a preview if testing shows people lose track of the first click. ## When to use Use a Date Range Picker when the two dates are one thing: a period to report on, a stay, a sprint. Both ends are set together, start never after end, and the value is complete or `null`. } doCaption="One field for one period: it cannot be half filled or set back to front." dont={} dontCaption="Two Date Pickers for one period: here the end is before the start, and nothing stops it." /> ## When not to use - **For one date.** Use a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs). - **When one end is optional**, such as a contract with no end date. The range needs both ends; use two Date Pickers and check their order yourself. ## Accessibility - As Date Picker: a labelled text box, an error state with the expected pattern, and the calendars in a dialog named "Choose dates". Without a visible label, pass `aria-label` to name the input. - The calendar button is named "Choose dates", with the current range when there is one. - `readOnly` works as on Date Picker: `readonly` on the input, no calendar button, and a click or Alt+Down opens nothing. - Every day in the range has `aria-selected`, so the span is announced, not only its ends. - A day of the month either side is decoration: hidden from assistive tech and not pickable, so each day is one button. - Presets are toggle buttons in a group named "Presets"; the one that matches the picked range is `aria-pressed`. - After both ends are in, the field goes back to rest, as Date Picker's does after a pick.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Field, FieldControl } from './Field' import { boxClass, inputStyles } from './InputField' import * as FieldStories from './Field.stories' # Field The label, required mark, info note and helper text for a control that has none of its own. Every Zweihänder control (Text Input, Select, Checkbox and the rest) already carries this anatomy. Field is for the control that does not: a native element the kit has no component for, a Base UI primitive, or one of your own. It wires the label, description and invalid state to it through Base UI Field. ## Variants There is one appearance. What changes is which optional parts are there. | Part | Use for | | --- | --- | | `helperText` | The format, limits or purpose, in a line; the error message when invalid. | | `labelInfo` | A longer rule or explanation most people do not need every time: behind an info button, so the form stays short. | | `validationState` | `error` when the value cannot be accepted: the helper text says what to change, and it and the edge turn red. `success` for a value checked and accepted. | | `required` | An asterisk after the label. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Field } from 'zweihander/field' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/field.json ``` - Source: [src/components/inputs/Field.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Field.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/text-input](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/text-input) (the label and helper parts) - Behaviour: [Base UI Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The control is whatever you put inside; in these stories it is a native time input in the same box as Text Input. ## Measurements The field is 20rem wide, capped at its container; with `isFullWidth` it fills the container. The info note is at most 22rem wide and opens above the button. ## Color ## States ), }, { label: 'Read-only', content: ( ), }, { label: 'Disabled', content: ( ), }, ]} > - **Hover** and **focus** belong to the control. The info button turns `--color-text` on hover and draws the `--color-border-focused` outline on keyboard focus. - **Error** colours the helper text, which then says what to change, and the edge of a field box inside. - **Read-only** is set on the control (`readOnly`), not on the Field. A field box with a read-only control inside is filled with `--color-background-input`; the edge, label and helper stay as they are. - **Disabled** disables the control; how it dims is the control's own. The info button stays active: the note may say why the field is disabled. ## API
`FieldControl` is Base UI's `Field.Control`: an `` by default, any element through `render`, with the label, description and invalid state wired to it. A Base UI control (Slider, Number Field, Checkbox) inside a Field wires itself. ### Differences from the spec - **No separate error part.** As in every Zweihänder control, the error is the helper text in the error state (the kit's API convention), so a field never shows a hint and an error at once. - **The info note is a toggletip**, opened by press or Enter, not a hover tooltip: tooltips do not open on touch. ## When to use Use a Field round a control that has no label of its own. Keep the helper text to a line; put a longer rule behind `labelInfo`. } doCaption="The format in a line under the control; the full rule behind the info button." dont={} dontCaption="A paragraph of helper text pushes every field below it down, on every visit." /> An **error** says what to change, not only that something is wrong. } doCaption="The error names the allowed range." dont={} dontCaption="'Invalid value' leaves people guessing what to change." /> ### Read-only A value people need to see but cannot change here (set by a rule, another team or their role) stays a field: put `readOnly` on the control and say in `helperText` why, and who can change it. Every Zweihänder control takes `readOnly`. The boxed fields (Text Input, Textarea, Search, Number Input, Select, Combobox, Date Picker, Date Range Picker) all look the same: a filled box, still focusable, the value selectable and submitted with the form. Checkbox, Radio, Switch and Rating keep their look, since their mark is the value, and only stop changing. } doCaption="Read-only: readable, focusable, copyable, and it says who can change it." dont={} dontCaption="Disabled: dimmed below readable contrast, skipped by Tab, not submitted." /> - **Not disabled.** A locked value is still read and copied; a disabled one is not (Disabled, below, is for "not yet"). - **No lock icon by default.** The fill already marks the state, and an icon would need its own name for screen readers; the helper text says more than a lock. - **A whole record that cannot be edited** is not a form of read-only fields: show it as a description list (`
`), label and value with no box. ### Disabled Disable a control only while it does not apply yet, and people can change that on the same screen: a choice earlier in the form, a step not done. Say what turns it on, in `helperText` or in the control that does it. } doCaption="Disabled for now, and the helper text says what turns it on." dont={} dontCaption="Nothing says why it is off or how to turn it on." /> - **Disable for "not yet", hide for "not you", read-only for "not changeable here".** An action or a field people's role never lets them use, and that they do not need to read, is left out, not shown disabled: a control they can never turn on is noise and a support ticket. A text input's own default width (about 20 characters) is its minimum otherwise, so it is zeroed here and the input grows back to fill the box. */} export const Fit = ({ children }) => (

) # File Uploader Choose files to send: drag them onto the drop zone or pick them with the button. It checks type, size and count, lists what was chosen, and shows progress or an error per file. It does not upload: your code does, and tells it how that is going. ## Variants | Mode | Use for | | --- | --- | | `multiple` | Attachments, a batch of photos: files are appended, up to `maxFiles`. | | Single | One document: an invoice, a CV. A new file replaces the chosen one, if it passes the checks. | Each file gets a type icon: a page with a coloured badge for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF, image and audio, after Microsoft 365, from the extension or MIME type. Anything else is the bare page. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { FileUploader } from 'zweihander/file-uploader' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/file-uploader.json ``` - Source: [src/components/inputs/FileUploader.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/FileUploader.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/file-uploader](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/file-uploader) - Behaviour: a native `` behind a kit [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Two more parts show only when needed: - **Errors**: one line per file that was not added, under the drop zone, e.g. "raw-scan.png is larger than 5 MB." - **File error**: in place of the progress ring, a short message from `getFileStatus`, e.g. "Upload failed". A long one truncates. ## Measurements One size. The buttons inside are `sm` Buttons, 24px tall. The uploader is 24rem wide unless `isFullWidth`. A file row has no inline padding, so its icon and remove button line up with the drop zone's edges. The type icon is 20px: a 13 × 18 page with a folded corner, and a badge 8px tall (14px wide, 16px for DOC and MP3) naming the type in 6px bold: DOC, XLS, PPT, PDF, IMG or MP3. ## Color The type badges keep fixed colours in both modes: they are each file type's identity, not the theme's, and white on each is above 4.5:1. The page is an 18% tint of the badge colour and the fold a 40% one; an unknown type gets a fixed light gray page (#e3e5e8, fold #c2c5cc). The Choose button is an `accent contained` Button and the remove buttons `secondary ghost`; their states are Button's. ## States }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, ]} > - **Dragging**: while a file is over the drop zone its edge turns solid `--color-border-focused` and it fills with `--color-background-neutral`, so the change is not colour alone. - **Rejected or required and empty**: the drop zone's edge turns `--color-text-danger` and the errors list why, one line per file. - **Focus** is the Choose button's and the remove buttons' own ring. - **Uploading**: a progress ring beside the remove button while `progress` is under 100; it goes at 100. An `error` takes its place. - **Disabled** fades the icon and the buttons, not the text: none of it is a native label, so faded text would fail contrast rather than be exempt. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
### Design notes - **Checks on every path in.** The system picker filters by `accept`, but a drop, or "All files" in the picker, does not. The uploader checks the type, size and count of everything and says why a file was left out. - **A rejected file never replaces a good one.** In single-file mode a new file replaces the chosen one only if it passes the checks. - **The same file twice is one file.** Name, size and modified time match, so it is skipped rather than listed again. - **Uploading is yours.** Start it in `onFilesChange` and report through `getFileStatus`. ## When to use Use a File Uploader to attach files to a form: receipts to a claim, documents to an application. Say what is allowed in `helperText`, and set `accept`, `maxSize` and `maxFiles` to match, so the rules are read before a file is turned away. } doCaption="The rules up front: types and size in the helper text, checked by accept and maxSize." dont={} dontCaption="No rules shown: people learn them one rejection at a time." /> Report upload progress per file with `getFileStatus`, and keep errors short ("Upload failed"): the row has room for a few words. ## When not to use - **For text people could paste.** Use a [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textarea--docs). - **For a link to a file.** Use a [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs) with `type="url"`. ## Accessibility - Dragging is a shortcut, never the only way: the Choose button is a real button, reached by Tab, and opens the system picker. The file input itself is hidden from assistive tech so there is one control, not two. - The uploader is a `group` named by its label; `required` adds "(required)" to that name, since a group cannot be `aria-required`. Submitting it empty shows "Choose at least one file." (or "Choose a file.") in the errors and moves focus to the Choose button, instead of the browser's bubble on the hidden input. - The helper text and any errors describe the Choose button, so they are read when focus lands on it. - The chosen files are a list named "Chosen files" ("Chosen file" when `multiple` is off), one item per file. - A polite status line announces "2 files added. 1 not added." and "report.pdf removed." - Remove buttons are named "Remove report.pdf". After a remove, focus moves to the next file's button, or back to Choose when the list is empty, so it is never lost. - The progress ring is a `progressbar` named "Uploading report.pdf", with its value. - While dragging, the drop zone's edge turns solid as well as changing colour.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { NumberInput } from './NumberInput' import * as NumberInputStories from './NumberInput.stories' # Number Input A number, typed or stepped: a quantity, a price, a count. The field is [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs)'s, with a decrease and an increase button inside it. ## Variants One appearance, the white outlined box. What changes is the size and how the number steps and is shown. | Size | Use for | | --- | --- | | `md` | Forms and dialogs: the default. | | `sm` | Dense places: a quantity in a cart row or a table cell. | | Setting | Use for | | --- | --- | | `min`, `max` | A range the value must stay in. The button at a limit is disabled. | | `step` | Values that move in fixed amounts: 5 minutes, 0.25 of a unit. | | `precision` | A fixed number of decimals, such as 2 for a price: `9.5` shows as `9.50`. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { NumberInput } from 'zweihander/number-input' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/number-input.json ``` - Source: [src/components/inputs/NumberInput.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/NumberInput.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/number-input](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/number-input) - Behaviour: [Base UI Number Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/number-field) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The steppers float inside the box: no divider, a small inset from its end, and a fill only on hover. ## Measurements The box is Text Input's: `sm` is 32px and `md` is 40px, one step taller than a Button. A stepper is a 24px square in both, centred in the box. The value sits 10px from the start edge and 8px before the steppers; the steppers are 2px apart and 6px from the end edge, so each icon sits 10px in. The input uses tabular figures, so digits do not shift as the value changes. ## Color The field's colours are Text Input's; the steppers add their own. ## States }, { label: 'Error', content: }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, ]} > - **Hover** on a stepper fills it with `--color-background-neutral` and darkens its icon; the field itself does not change. - **Focus** is the field's 2px ring around the whole box, in `--color-text-danger` when invalid. - **At a limit** the stepper that would go past it is disabled, at 50% opacity, and ignores hover, so it looks as unavailable as it is. - **Read-only** fills the box with `--color-background-input`; the steppers do nothing. - **Disabled** dims the whole field to 50%. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`ref` goes to the input. `id` and `className` are passed through too; no other attributes are. ### Differences from the spec - **No `filled` appearance.** The spec's filled field (a tinted box with a bottom rule) was dropped to match the Claude apps, where every field is the white outlined box. - **Two sizes, not three.** `sm` (32px) and `md` (40px), after Atlassian Design: a field is one step taller than a button, so `sm` lines up with a Button in a toolbar. The spec's largest step was dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box. - **`onValueChange` with a number**, not `onChange`: built on Base UI, it takes Base UI's name, and the value arrives parsed rather than as text. - **`max` is optional with no default.** The spec marks it required with a default of 100, which contradicts itself; a quantity with no upper bound is common. - **`label`, `helperText`, `validationState`** are added from the shared field. ## When to use Use a Number Input for a quantity people adjust by a little, or type outright: guests, items in a cart, minutes, a price. Set `min` and `max` whenever the range is known, so the steppers stop at its ends. } doCaption="A quantity, nudged up and down within a known range." dont={} dontCaption="A postcode is not a quantity: stepping it is meaningless, and formatting may change it." /> ## When not to use - **For numbers that are identifiers**: postcodes, card numbers, phone numbers, IDs. Use a [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs) with `inputMode="numeric"`, which brings up the number keyboard without steppers or formatting. - **For a value picked on a scale**, such as volume or a percentage people judge by eye. Use a Slider. - **For a small fixed set of numbers** (1, 2 or 4 seats). Use radios or a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs). ## Accessibility - The input is a text field with `inputmode="numeric"` and the role description "Number field", named by the label. Without a visible label, pass `aria-label`: a placeholder is a hint, not a name. - **Keyboard:** Up and Down step the value by `step` from the input; with Shift they step by 10, with Alt by 0.1. The steppers are out of the tab order (`tabindex="-1"`): the arrow keys do the same from the field. - The steppers are named "Increase" and "Decrease" and are disabled at the limits, so a screen reader hears why nothing happened. - The value is parsed and formatted in the user's locale; the form receives the plain number. - `helperText` is the input's description and `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid`, as on Text Input. - Steppers widen to 44px on touch screens, the one direction they can grow without covering the input or each other.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { OTPInput } from './OTPInput' import * as OTPInputStories from './OTPInput.stories' # OTP Input A short one-time code, typed or pasted into a row of single-character cells: the code from a text message, an email or an authenticator app. ## Variants One appearance, a row of small outlined boxes. What changes is the size, whether the cells are grouped, and whether there is a resend button. | Size | Use for | | --- | --- | | `md` | Sign-in, verification and confirmation screens: the default. | | `sm` | A code asked for inside a dense panel or a table row. | | Setting | Use for | | --- | --- | | `groupSize` | A code people read in chunks: `3` shows six digits as 3 – 3, `4` an eight-character backup code as 4 – 4. | | `onResend` | A code that was sent and may not arrive. The button waits `resendCooldown` seconds, showing the time left. Return a promise: a failed send starts no cooldown. | | `validationType` | `numeric` for codes from texts and apps; `alphanumeric` for backup and recovery codes. | | `mask` | A code that should not be read over someone's shoulder. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { OTPInput } from 'zweihander/otp-input' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/otp-input.json ``` - Source: [src/components/inputs/OTPInput.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/OTPInput.tsx) - Spec: none on uiguideline.com; the reference is [shadcn/ui Input OTP](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/input-otp) - Behaviour: [Base UI OTP Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/otp-field) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Each cell is its own box with the field's edge, fill and radius, so the row reads as several small fields that belong together. The label and helper text are Text Input's. ## Measurements A cell is a square as tall as a Text Input of the same size: 32px in `sm`, 40px in `md`. The digit is Heading lg (24/28, semibold) in both; the separator between groups is body type. The characters use tabular figures, centred in the cell. The resend button is a small ghost [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs). ## Color `--field-edge` is the shared field's edge colour: `--color-border-input` by default, `--color-text-danger` on error and `--color-text-success` on success, so every cell and the helper text change together. ## States }, { label: 'Error', content: }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, ]} > - **Hover** changes nothing: a cell is a text field, and the caret shows where typing goes. - **Focus** rings only the cell being typed into, in `--color-text-danger` when invalid. - **Error** turns every cell's edge and the helper text `--color-text-danger`. - **Read-only** fills the cells with `--color-background-input`; typing does nothing. - **Disabled** dims the cells to 50% and disables the resend button. - **Cooling down**, the resend button is disabled and shows the time left as `m:ss`. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`ref` goes to the first cell. `id` and `className` are passed through too; no other attributes are. ### Differences from the spec There is no uiguideline.com spec for this component; the reference is shadcn/ui Input OTP. - **One component, flat props.** shadcn composes `InputOTP`, `InputOTPGroup`, `InputOTPSlot` and `InputOTPSeparator`; Zweihänder takes `length` and `groupSize`, as the API conventions ask for flat props before 1.0. - **Resend is built in.** shadcn leaves it to the page. Every screen that sends a code needs the same button and countdown, so it lives here. - **Real inputs, one per cell**, from Base UI, not one hidden input under drawn slots: each cell is focusable and named. - **`label`, `helperText`, `validationState`** are added from the shared field. ## When to use Use an OTP Input for a short code someone copies from another place: a text message, an email, an authenticator app. Say where the code was sent in `helperText`, and give a way to send another. } doCaption="Six digits, labelled, with where the code went and a way to resend it." dont={} dontCaption="Sixteen cells are too many to scan or correct. A long key is one Text Input." /> ## When not to use - **For codes longer than about 8 characters**, licence keys or recovery phrases. Use a [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs). - **For a PIN or password people make up themselves.** Use a [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs) with `type="password"`: cells suggest a code that was sent. - **For a number people adjust.** Use a [Number Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-numberinput--docs). ## Accessibility - The cells sit in a `group` named by the label; the label also names the first cell, and each later cell is named by `slotLabel`, "Character 2 of 6" by default. - **Keyboard:** the group is one tab stop: only the cell to type into is in the tab order. Typing a character fills the cell and moves to the next; Backspace clears the cell before and moves back; Left and Right move between cells. - Characters `validationType` does not allow are dropped, so letters cannot enter a numeric code. - Pasting the whole code into any cell fills every cell; spaces are ignored. - The first cell has `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so phones offer the code from a text message. - `helperText` is the group's description and `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid` on every cell. - The resend button is disabled during the cooldown and its name carries the time left. After a send, focus moves to the first cell, so it is not lost with the disabled button; while a send is pending the button stays focusable and is marked `aria-busy`. The countdown is not a live region, so it does not interrupt every second.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { PasswordInput, defaultPasswordRules } from './PasswordInput' import * as PasswordInputStories from './PasswordInput.stories' # Password Input A password field with a Show / Hide button and, where a password is being chosen, the rules it must meet, ticked off as the reader types. ## Variants One appearance, Text Input's. What changes is whether the password is being typed or chosen. | Use | Setting | | --- | --- | | Signing in, or confirming who you are before a change | The default: `autoComplete="current-password"`, no rules. | | Choosing a password: sign up, reset, change | `autoComplete="new-password"` and `rules`, so password managers suggest one and the reader sees what it needs. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { PasswordInput, defaultPasswordRules } from 'zweihander/password-input' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/password-input.json ``` - Source: [src/components/inputs/PasswordInput.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/PasswordInput.tsx) - Spec: none on uiguideline.com; the rules follow [NIST SP 800-63B](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html) (length over character kinds) - Built on: [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs) and its `TextInputButton` - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The field, label, helper text and button are Text Input's; this component adds the rules and the button's behaviour. ## Measurements Field sizes are Text Input's, except at the end: the Show / Hide button is a plain word inside the box, with no fill or divider, 6px each side of it and 4px from the edge, running the box's full height. The rules sit in its helper text, one per line. ## Color A rule not yet met takes the helper text's colour. A met rule stays green when the field is in error: it is done. ## States }, { label: 'Error', content: }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, ]} > - **Hover and focus** are Text Input's; the Show button has no fill on hover, and its focus ring is drawn inside its own edge. - **Shown**, the field is `type="text"` and the button reads Hide. It goes back to dots when the form is sent. - **Error** colours the edge and the helper text `--color-text-danger`; met rules stay green. - **Disabled** dims the field and disables the button. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other Text Input prop and input attribute passes through, except `type`, `suffix` and `endAddon`, which the component owns. `ref` points at the input. `defaultPasswordRules` and the `PasswordRule` type are exported with it. ### Differences from the spec There is no uiguideline.com spec for this component. It moved here from the auth templates, where it was a template file, when Settings became its first use outside sign-in. ## When to use Use it for every password field: sign in, sign up, reset, and change password in Settings. The field is [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs)'s. It searches one place: a list, a table, a results page. ## Variants One appearance, the white outlined box, in two sizes, with or without a visible label. | Size | Use for | | --- | --- | | `md` | Above a list or a page of results: the default. | | `sm` | Toolbars and table headers: as tall as a default Button. | | Label | Use for | | --- | --- | | None (default) | A search box whose place makes its purpose plain: a page header, above a list. It is named "Search", or by `aria-label`. | | `label` | A search inside a form, among other labelled fields. | | Shortcut | Use for | | --- | --- | | None (default) | Most fields. | | `shortcut="/"` | The one search a page is about, such as the search above a list page's table. The key cap shows while the field is empty and idle. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Search } from 'zweihander/search' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/search.json ``` - Source: [src/components/inputs/Search.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Search.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/search](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/search) - Behaviour: [Base UI Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The placeholder is the input's, "Search" unless given. The browser's own clear control is hidden, so there are not two. Not numbered above: with `shortcut`, a [Kbd](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-kbd--docs) key cap sits where the clear button goes, while the field is empty and not focused; the two never show at once. ## Measurements The box is Text Input's: `sm` is 32px and `md` is 40px, one step taller than a Button. The search icon and the clear button's icon are 16px in both; the clear button is a 24px target round its icon. The start padding is 10px, as Text Input's; the end is 6px, so the clear button's icon still sits 10px from the edge. 20rem wide, capped at its container, or the container's width with `isFullWidth`. ## Color Search has no validation state; its field colours are Text Input's default ones. ## States }, { label: 'Clear hover', pseudo: 'hover', content: }, { label: 'With a shortcut', content: }, { label: 'Read-only', content: }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, ]} > - **The clear button** appears once there is a query, and not while the field is disabled or read-only. On hover its icon darkens to `--color-text`. - **Focus** is the field's 2px `--color-border-focused` outline around the box, on click as well as keyboard. The clear button, when tabbed to, draws its own ring instead, so the two never double. - **The shortcut's key cap** shows while the field is empty and hides on focus, when the key would type instead. Disabled or read-only, there is no key cap and the key is not bound. - **Read-only** fills the box with `--color-background-input`. - **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `` attribute passes through, including `ref`, `name`, `autoFocus` and `onKeyDown`. `type` is always `search`. ### Differences from the spec - **No `filled` appearance.** The spec's filled field (a tinted box with a bottom rule) was dropped to match the Claude apps, where every field is the white outlined box. - **Two sizes, not three.** `sm` (32px) and `md` (40px), after Atlassian Design: a field is one step taller than a button, so `sm` lines up with a Button in a toolbar. The spec's largest step was dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box. - **`label` and `size` are added**, from the shared field, so a search box can match the form or toolbar it sits in. - **`value` is added** for a controlled query. - **`shortcut` is added**, a single key that focuses the field. - **No suggestion panel.** Recent searches and results grouped by type, as the spec's global search shows them, are left to the app; picking one value from matches is the [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs)'s job. Search stays a field, so there are not two lists that behave alike. - Native `disabled`, `readOnly` names. ## When to use Use Search to find or filter: a list of components, a table, the whole site. Say in the placeholder what is searched. } doCaption="A Search field: a searchbox to assistive tech, with a clear button and Escape to clear." dont={} dontCaption="A Text Input with a search icon looks the same but is a plain textbox, with no way to clear it." /> When it searches the site, put it inside a `
` (or ``) so it becomes a landmark people can jump to. The component is only the field: filtering a list in place does not need a landmark. Give the page's main search `shortcut="/"`, and only that one. ## When not to use - **To find anything from anywhere in the app**, with recent items and results grouped by type. That is a command palette, opened with ⌘K, and the kit does not ship one. Do not bind ⌘K to a Search. - **To choose one value from a list.** Use a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs): it shows the matches and keeps the choice. - **For other free text.** Use a [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs). ## Accessibility - `type="search"`, exposed as a `searchbox`, named by the visible label or "Search". What changes is the size, what sits beside the value, and the validation state. | Size | Use for | | --- | --- | | `md` | Forms and dialogs: the default. | | `sm` | Dense places: toolbars, table filters, inline edits. As tall as a default Button. | | Affix | Use for | | --- | --- | | `prefix` | A fixed start the value continues: "https://", a currency sign, an icon that says what the field holds. | | `suffix` | A unit the value is measured in: "kg", "%", "days". | **Add-ons** are filled segments joined to the edge of the box, divided from the value by a hairline. The label and helper are 12px in both sizes, the label in bold (`--font-weight-label`, 653, as Atlassian's form Label): only the box changes height. A button in `prefix` or `suffix` is a 24px target round its icon. The field is 20rem wide, capped at its container; with `isFullWidth` it fills the container. The edge is 1px. An add-on runs the full height of the box, and its 1px divider takes the edge's colour, so a field in the error state is red all round, divider included. ## Color The field has no colour variants. Its validation state changes the edge and the helper text together. Switch the theme in the toolbar: the values follow. ## States }, { label: 'Error', content: }, { label: 'Read-only', content: }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, ]} > - **Hover** changes nothing: the field is already plainly a field, and the cursor turns to a text cursor. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the box, drawn on click as well as from the keyboard, since that is where typing will go. The placeholder is the textarea's, in `--color-text-subtlest`. ## Measurements A textarea grows, so it has no height token: it takes block padding instead, after Atlassian's textarea: 2px in `sm` and 6px in `md`. Both sizes take body type and 10px of inline padding, as every field's box, so the text starts 11px from the outer edge. The starting height is `minRows` lines (3 by default) plus that padding. The padding sits on the textarea, not the box, so the resize handle lands in the field's corner. 20rem wide, capped at its container, or the container's width with `isFullWidth`. With `maxRows`, the input stops at that many lines plus its padding, whether it grew by itself or was dragged. ## Color The same colours as Text Input: no colour variants, and the validation state changes the edge and the helper text together. ## States }, { label: 'Read-only', content:

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { ProgressBar } from './ProgressBar' import * as ProgressBarStories from './ProgressBar.stories' # Progress Bar Shows how far a task with a known size has got: an upload, an install, the steps of a setup. ## Variants `variant` is the colour of the fill, by meaning. The track is the same in all four. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `primary` | The default: a task the user started and is waiting on. | | `accent` | A strong fill in neutral black or white, where the brand colour would clash or already means something else. | | `secondary` | Low emphasis: progress in the background, or one of many bars in a list. | | `destructive` | A task that is failing, or a quota about to run out. | `size` is the track's thickness, and `isRounded` gives it pill ends. When a task has started but its size is not known yet, go indeterminate, and switch to a value as soon as there is one. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { ProgressBar } from 'zweihander/progress-bar' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/progress-bar.json ``` - Source: [src/components/loaders/ProgressBar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/loaders/ProgressBar.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/progress-bar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/progress-bar) - Behaviour: [Base UI Progress](https://base-ui.com/react/components/progress) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy ## Measurements The bar fills the width of its container. Each size sets only the track's height. The value label is at least 4 characters wide, so the bar does not jump as the number grows from 9% to 100%. ## Color The fill is what carries the value, so it must clear 3:1 against the track. Not every accent's solid does (amber's is about 2.9:1 on white), so each variant fills with a colour meant to be read as text on the page, which keeps it at 3:1 or better on the track. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. ## States A progress bar is not interactive: it has no hover, focus or pressed state. }, { label: 'Complete', content: }, ]} > - **Progress** fills from the start edge, easing between values over `--duration-slow`. - **Indeterminate** slides 40% of the track across, once every 1.4s. The value label is hidden: there is no value to show. - **Complete** is a full bar. It does not change on its own; replace or remove it when the task ends. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other prop goes to Base UI's `Progress.Root`: `id`, `aria-labelledby`, `min`, `format`, `locale`, `getAriaValueText`. ### Differences from the spec - **`max`, not `maxValue`**, the name Base UI and the native `` use. ## When to use Use a Progress Bar for a task that takes long enough to wait on and whose size is known, or will be: an upload, an import, the steps of a setup. Name the task in the `label`. } doCaption="The label names the task, so the reader knows what they are waiting for." dont={} dontCaption="A bare bar leaves sighted readers guessing what it measures, even with an aria-label." /> `value` is out of `max`, and the value label shows the percentage: Without a visible label, `aria-label` names the bar for screen readers. Use it only where the context already says what the bar measures. ## When not to use - **For a short wait with no known size.** Use a [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-loaders-spinner--docs). - **For content whose shape you know.** A [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-loaders-skeleton--docs) keeps the layout. - **For steps the user moves through themselves.** Use a [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-navigation-stepper--docs): it names the steps, and the user can go back. ## Accessibility - `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuetext` from Base UI. Indeterminate drops `aria-valuenow` rather than reporting 0. - Every bar needs a name: a visible `label` (linked by Base UI) or `aria-label`. - The fill clears 3:1 on the track for every variant and accent, in both modes. The value label is `--color-text-subtlest`. - Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the fill stops easing between values and the indeterminate slide slows from 1.4s to 4s a pass. - A progressbar is not a live region. If completion matters, announce it (a Toast, or a status message) when the task ends.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Skeleton } from './Skeleton' import * as SkeletonStories from './Skeleton.stories' {/* On the page background: in dark mode --color-background-neutral is the stage's own colour. */} export const card = { background: 'var(--color-surface)', padding: 'var(--space-4)', borderRadius: 'var(--radius-lg)' } # Skeleton A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading, so the page keeps its layout and the reader sees what is coming. ## Variants `appearance` sets the corners, to match what the shape stands in for. Any appearance takes any size. | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | `circle` | An avatar or a round icon. Its height is its width. | | `square` | The default: an image, a media block, anything with square corners. | | `rounded` | Text, buttons and cards: anything with the kit's rounded corners. | `rows` stacks lines of text, the last one shorter so it reads as a paragraph rather than a block. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Skeleton } from 'zweihander/skeleton' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/skeleton.json ``` - Source: [src/components/loaders/Skeleton.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/loaders/Skeleton.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/skeleton](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/skeleton) - Behaviour: a plain element; there is no behaviour here worth Base UI - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy A skeleton is built from shapes like these, placed by the page in the layout of the content that will replace them. ## Measurements A skeleton has no sizes: `width` and `height` copy the content it stands in for. These are the defaults, and the parts it sizes itself. The default width is the container's. The last of several `rows` is 60% of the width. ## Color Every shape is one colour, the same subtle surface as a hover. It is below any contrast floor on purpose: a placeholder should read as "something goes here", not compete with content that has arrived. Switch the theme in the toolbar: the value follows. ## States A skeleton is not interactive: it has no hover, focus or pressed state. }, ]} >
- **Static** is the default. - **Pulsing**, with `hasAnimation`, fades to 50% and back every 1.6s. It stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through to the outer element. ## When to use Use a Skeleton when you know the shape of what is loading: a list, a card, a profile. Match the shapes to the content that will replace them, with the same sizes and the same gaps. } doCaption="Shapes of the content that is coming: the layout holds when it arrives." dont={} dontCaption="One block for a whole card jumps to a different layout on load, which is worse than a spinner." /> Animate the few shapes that matter, or none: `hasAnimation` is off by default because a screen of pulsing shapes is noise. ## When not to use - **When you do not know the shape of what is coming.** Use a [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-loaders-spinner--docs). - **For a long task with a known size.** Use a [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs). - **For a load that is usually instant.** A skeleton that flashes for 200ms is noise; show nothing, or a Spinner with a `delay`. ## Accessibility - **A skeleton is decoration** and is `aria-hidden`, with its `rows` hidden as one. It says nothing to a screen reader. - The region it stands in for has to say it is loading: put `aria-busy="true"` on it, as the CardPlaceholder story does, and remove it when the content arrives. - If the wait matters, announce it: a visually hidden status, or a Spinner with a label. - `--color-background-neutral` is below 3:1 on the page in both modes, on purpose. It is not content, and should not compete with content that has arrived. - The pulse stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Spinner } from './Spinner' import * as SpinnerStories from './Spinner.stories' # Spinner Says that something is loading when there is no telling how long it will take, or, given a value, how far along it is. ## Variants `variant` is the colour of the indicator. The track and the label are the same in all three. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `accent` | The default: a quiet placeholder in `--color-text`, inside content that has its own colour. | | `primary` | A load the page is about, where the brand colour helps it be found: the first load of a view. | | `secondary` | Low emphasis: a spinner beside other muted text, or in a dense list. | With a `value` it stops spinning and becomes a progress ring, which reads better than a bar in a small space such as a thumbnail. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Spinner } from 'zweihander/spinner' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/spinner.json ``` - Source: [src/components/loaders/Spinner.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/loaders/Spinner.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/spinner](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/spinner) - Behaviour: a plain element; there is no behaviour here worth Base UI - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy While spinning, the indicator is 30% of the ring turning once every `--duration-spin`. With no `label`, a visually hidden "Loading" stands in for it. ## Measurements The ring is a 2.25px stroke at every size, its outer edge on the box's edge. There is no token for 2.25px, so the thickness is not in the tables. ## Color The indicator is the part that has to be seen, so each variant takes a colour that clears 3:1 on the page. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. ## States A spinner is not interactive: it has no hover, focus or pressed state. }, { label: 'Complete', content: }, ]} > - **Spinning** is the default, and what it shows with `isIndeterminate` even when given a `value`. - **Progress** fills the ring clockwise from twelve o'clock, easing between values over `--duration-slow`. - **Delayed**: with `delay`, nothing shows until it has passed. The live region is in the page, empty, from the start. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `` attribute passes through to the outer element. ## When to use Use a Spinner when something is loading and you cannot say what its result will look like or how long it will take. Use one per region that is loading, labelled with what is coming. } doCaption="One spinner for the region, named for what is coming." dont={} dontCaption="A spinner per card says the same thing three times, and three screen-reader announcements." /> Give a load you expect to be fast a `delay` of 300–500ms. The spinner only appears if the wait turns out to be long enough to notice. ## When not to use - **When you know the shape of what is coming.** A [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-loaders-skeleton--docs) keeps the layout and says more. - **For a long task with a known size**: an upload, an install. Use a [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs), or a `value` here when space is tight. - **Inside a button.** Use the Button's `isLoading`: it keeps the button's width and focus and stops a second click. ## Accessibility - **Spinning, it is `role="status"`**, a polite live region, named by `label` or "Loading". The region renders empty and its text (the label, or a visually hidden "Loading") is inserted just after, or once `delay` has passed: screen readers announce text added to a live region that is already in the page, not a region that mounts full. - **With a value, it is `role="progressbar"`** with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin="0"` and `aria-valuemax="100"`. Values outside 0–100 are clamped. - The SVG is hidden. - The indicator clears 3:1 on the page in every variant: `--color-text-brand` (measured at 4.5:1 per accent), `--color-text-subtlest`, `--color-text`. The track is decoration and may be faint. - Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it slows to one turn in 2.5s rather than stopping, since a frozen arc reads as "stuck", and the progress ring stops easing between values. - Put `aria-busy="true"` on the region that is loading, and remove the spinner when the load ends, so the change is announced.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as BreadcrumbsStories from './Breadcrumbs.stories' # Breadcrumbs The trail from the top of a hierarchy down to the current page, each step a link back up. ## Variants Breadcrumbs has one look. What changes is the size, how a long trail collapses, and what sits between the steps. | Form | Use for | | --- | --- | | `md` | Under a page title, at body size. The default. | | `sm` | Dense headers, panels and side sheets, at `body-sm`. | | `maxItems` | Deep hierarchies, or a trail in a narrow place: the middle collapses to "…", which expands in place. | | `separator` | A slash or other glyph, where a chevron would clash with nearby icons. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Breadcrumbs } from 'zweihander/breadcrumbs' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/breadcrumbs.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Breadcrumbs.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Breadcrumbs.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/breadcrumbs](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/breadcrumbs) - Behaviour: a plain `
` and `
    `, after the [APG breadcrumb pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Each step is a list item: its link (or the ellipsis), then a separator. The last item has no separator after it. ## Measurements Breadcrumbs is text, not a row of controls. At `md` each item sits in a 24px box around its 14/20 text, with 8px either side of the separator, as Atlassian Design's breadcrumb items. Atlassian Design has no small breadcrumb; `sm` is the kit's own, and its height is its line height. The separator icon is 1em: it follows the text size. ## Color One colour set. Switch the theme in the toolbar: the values follow. ## States - **Hover** turns a link to `--color-text` and underlines it; on the ellipsis it fills an `--color-background-neutral` chip. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the link or the ellipsis. - There is no disabled state: a level the reader cannot open is left out of the trail. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
    Every other `
    ` attribute passes through. ## When to use Use Breadcrumbs on pages three or more levels deep, under the page title, so a reader can see where they are and jump back up any number of levels. It is a secondary aid: the main navigation still has to get people everywhere. Keep the trail on one line. When it would wrap, collapse the middle with `maxItems`; the first level and the nearest ones stay in view. } doCaption="Collapse a long trail with maxItems: one line, and the levels that matter most stay visible." dont={} dontCaption="A trail that wraps reads as two rows and pushes the page down." /> Write each label as the title of the page it opens, short enough to scan. The last item is the current page, as text: a link to the page you are on does nothing useful. ## When not to use - **For history.** Breadcrumbs shows where a page sits, not how the reader got there. For "go back", use a Back link or [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs). - **On a flat site.** One or two levels need no trail; the main navigation already says where you are. - **For the steps of a task.** Use a Stepper: it shows the steps ahead too, and which are done. - **As the main navigation.** Use a side navigation of links, or Tabs. ## Accessibility - A `
    ` landmark named "Breadcrumb" (change it with `aria-label`), around an ordered list: screen readers announce the number of items and the position of each. - Each level above the current page is a real ``, in the tab order. - The last item is text with `aria-current="page"`, not a link. - Separators are `aria-hidden`, so they are not read between items. - The ellipsis is a button named "Show 3 more". Enter or Space expands the trail and moves focus to the first item it revealed, rather than dropping it on the page. - The ellipsis is under 44px; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) its hit area grows to 44×44px without it growing. - Focus ring: 2px `--color-border-focused`, 2px offset.

components-navigation-link.name: Link

variant.description: Colour. `accent` is the foreground, as on Button; `secondary` is muted, for footers and meta text.

size.description: Omit to inherit the surrounding text size, which is what a link inside a sentence wants.

underline.description: `always` inside running text: colour alone does not mark a link. `hover` only where the context already says "these are links", like a nav list.

isExternal.description: Opens in a new tab, with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, an external icon and "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers.

isDisabled.description: Rendered without `href`, so it cannot navigate; `aria-disabled` says why.

render.description: Replaces the rendered element, e.g. a router's `<Link />`.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Link } from './Link' import * as LinkStories from './Link.stories' # Link Text that takes you somewhere: another page, a section of this one, an outside site. It navigates; it does not act. ## Variants `variant` is the colour; `underline` says whether the line shows at rest. Any variant takes either underline. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | Primary | Links in running text and on their own. The default. | | Accent | Links in the foreground colour, where the brand colour would compete: dense lists, navigation. | | Secondary | Footers, captions and meta text, where the link is not the point. | | Underline | Use for | | --- | --- | | Always | Inside running text, where only the line tells a link from the words around it. The default. | | Hover | Places that are obviously lists of links: a nav list, a footer column. | Without a `size`, a link takes the size of the sentence around it, which is what a link in text wants. `sm`, `md` and `lg` are for links that stand alone. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Link } from 'zweihander/link' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/link.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Link.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Link.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/link](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/link) - Behaviour: a native ``; `render` from [Base UI useRender](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/use-render) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The underline is a text decoration on the link itself, 1px thick and offset 0.2em below the text. ## Measurements Each size sets only the text; without one, the link inherits it. The text is medium weight. The external icon is 0.9em, so it scales with the text, with 0.2em before it. ## Color The text and its underline share one colour. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. ## States }, ]} > - **Hover** thickens the underline from 1px to 2px and keeps the colour, so the link keeps the contrast it was measured at. With `underline="hover"`, hover is when the line appears. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the text. - **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity, with no `href`. - There is no visited style: most links in an app lead to screens, not documents, and a "seen it" colour there is noise. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `` attribute passes through, including `ref`, `target` and `rel`. ## When to use Use a Link to go somewhere: another page, a section of this one, a file, an outside site. Inside a sentence, keep the underline; let the link text say where it goes, so it still makes sense read on its own. } doCaption="The link text names the destination: it reads on its own, in a screen reader's list of links too." dont={} dontCaption={'"Click here" says nothing out of context, and hides where the link goes.'} /> Mark links that leave for another site with `isExternal` only when they open a new tab, and keep that rare: a new tab breaks the Back button. With a router, pass its link as `render`. Link merges its class and props onto it, and the router keeps control of navigation: ```tsx }>Settings ``` ## When not to use - **For an action.** Saving, deleting or opening a dialog is a [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs). A link-styled action looks like it will take you away, and does not respond to Space. - **For a prominent call to action that navigates.** Use a Button with `href`: it renders an `` with the weight of a button. - **For a trail of parent pages.** Use Breadcrumbs. - **For moving through pages of a list.** Use Pagination. ## Accessibility - A real ``, so it is in the tab order, opens with Enter, and shows up in a screen reader's list of links. - Underlined by default: colour alone does not mark a link for someone who cannot tell the colours apart (WCAG 1.4.1). - `isExternal` adds "(opens in a new tab)" to the accessible name, and sets `rel="noopener noreferrer"`: a new tab that opens without warning strands people who cannot see it happen. - `isDisabled` removes `href`, the only thing that stops an `` navigating, drops the click handlers and sets `aria-disabled`. Without an `href` it leaves the tab order. Prefer hiding a link that cannot be followed, or saying in text why it is unavailable. - Every variant is a text colour measured at 4.5:1 on the page, and hover does not change it. - Focus ring: 2px `--color-border-focused`, 2px offset.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as MenuStories from './Menu.stories' # Menu A list of actions that opens from a button: the "…" on a row, an "Actions" dropdown, a "View" menu of toggles. It acts or toggles; to pick a value for a form, use a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs). ## Variants Menu has one look. What changes is the kind of entry in `items`, and a menu can mix them: | Entry | Use for | | --- | --- | | Action (the default) | Something to do now: Edit, Duplicate, Delete. Closes the menu. `isDestructive` draws it in the danger colour. | | Link (`href`) | Going somewhere: Documentation, Settings. A real ``. | | Submenu (`items`) | A set of choices that belongs under one item: Move to, Share with. | | Checkbox (`type: 'checkbox'`) | Settings that are on or off, several at a time: Show hidden files. Keeps the menu open. | | Radio (`type: 'radio'`) | One of a few settings: Sort by name, date or size. Keeps the menu open. | | Group (`type: 'group'`) and separator | Structure for a longer menu: a label over related items, a rule between sets. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Menu } from 'zweihander/menu' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/menu.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Menu.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Menu.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/menu](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/menu) - Behaviour: [Base UI Menu](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy A link item has the same parts as an action. Checkbox and radio items show a check where an action shows its icon, so their labels line up. ## Measurements The item follows Atlassian Design's dropdown item: 8px block and 12px inline padding around a 20px line, so a one-line item is 36px tall. The box ramp has no 36px step, so the md control tier (32px) is the floor and the padding makes the rest. Items sit 4px inside the popup's border and 2px apart, with a 6px corner and 12px between icon and label; a shortcut or a chevron sits 24px after the label; a separator is as wide as the items, with 4px above and below; a group label has 8px block padding, 12px before and 24px after. The popup is at least 12rem wide, or the trigger's width if that is wider, and no taller than the space on screen: past that it scrolls. It opens 4px from the trigger. ## Color The destructive item uses the danger text colour, not the solid: it reads at 4.5:1 on the popup and on its highlight. ## States }, { label: 'Open', content: }, ]} /> - **Highlighted** is where the arrow keys or the pointer are: a `--color-background-neutral` fill; the icon keeps `--color-text-subtlest`. A submenu's item stays highlighted while its submenu is open. Focus moves with the highlight, so there is no separate focus ring inside the popup. - **Disabled** items are muted at 60% opacity and skipped by the arrow keys (Archive, above). - **Checked** checkbox and radio items show the check; unchecked ones keep the empty column. - The trigger's own hover, focus and pressed states are the [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs)'s. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`items` is data, like Select's `options`, not child components. `shortcut` is display only: binding the key is left to the page, which knows what else is bound. ## When to use Use a Menu for actions that belong to one thing but would crowd the screen as buttons: the actions on a table row, a card's overflow, a toolbar's "More". Keep it short, put the most used item first, and give destructive actions the last place, after a separator. } doCaption="Delete last, after a separator, in the danger colour." dont={} dontCaption="Delete between two everyday actions: one arrow key too far and it is chosen." /> } doCaption="A menu of actions. Each item does something now." dont={} dontCaption="A menu standing in for a form field. Use a Select: it has a label, a value and a form name." /> The popup opens below the trigger, lined up with its start edge; `side` and `align` place it elsewhere. ## When not to use - **To pick a value for a form.** Use a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs), or a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs) when the list is long enough to search. - **For one or two actions.** Show them as [Buttons](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs): a hidden action is one fewer person finds. - **For the app's main navigation.** Use a side navigation of [Links](?path=/docs/components-navigation-link--docs) or [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs), which show where the reader is. - **For content: a form, a preview.** Use a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs). A menu holds only menu items. ## Accessibility - The trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; the popup is a `role="menu"` of `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and `menuitemradio`, with `aria-checked` on the toggles and `aria-disabled` on disabled items. - Keyboard: Enter, Space or Arrow Down on the trigger opens it; arrows move (disabled items are skipped), typing a few letters jumps to the matching item, Enter selects, Arrow Right opens a submenu and Arrow Left closes it, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. - Toggles keep the menu open, so several can be changed in one go; actions close it and focus returns to the trigger. - The icon and shortcut are hidden from assistive tech; the label names the item. Give `textValue` when a label is not plain text, or typeahead cannot find it. - A disabled link has no `href`, so it cannot be followed. - Items are 36px tall, 44px on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`). - `isModal` (the default) makes the rest of the page inert while the menu is open, so a screen reader stays in the menu.

components-navigation-menubar--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as MenubarStories from './Menubar.stories' # Menubar A row of menus across the top of a tool, as in a desktop app: File, Edit, View, each opening a flyout of commands. Use it in an editor-like screen with more commands than a toolbar can show. ## Variants Menubar has one look. Each flyout is a [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) popup and takes the same entries: actions with shortcuts, links, submenus, checkbox and radio items, groups and separators. | Menu | Use for | | --- | --- | | Enabled (the default) | Commands that apply now. | | Disabled (`disabled`) | A menu that does not apply in the current state. It stays in place, muted, so the bar does not shift. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Menubar } from 'zweihander/menubar' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/menubar.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Menubar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Menubar.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/menu](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/menu) - Behaviour: [Base UI Menubar](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menubar) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The flyout on this tab is a picture: it is drawn open in place, not positioned over the page. Its parts are Menu's; see [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) for the item's own anatomy. ## Measurements The bar is a strip: its triggers are rows of the sm control tier (24px), shorter than the 36px items in the flyout. Atlassian Design has no menubar, so the bar follows the Figma library; the flyouts are Menu's. The bar has no fill, border or padding: it is its triggers side by side, touching, each with the sm control's corner. Labels are regular weight. A flyout opens 4px below its trigger, lined up with the trigger's start edge. When the bar is wider than its container, it scrolls sideways. ## Color The flyout's colours are Menu's. ## States }, { label: 'Open', content: }, { label: 'Disabled menu', content: }, ]} /> - **Hover and highlighted**: the trigger takes the same `--color-background-neutral` fill as a highlighted item in the flyout. - **Open**: the trigger keeps that fill while its flyout is open, so the reader sees which menu they are in. - **Focus**: a keyboard focus ring inside the trigger, so it does not collide with its neighbours. - **Disabled**: muted at 60% opacity, no fill on hover, skipped by the arrow keys. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`menus` is data, and each menu's `items` is Menu's `items`. Shortcuts are plain trailing text, as in Menu: display only, binding the key is left to the page. ### Differences from the spec - **No navigation menu.** The source pairs a menubar with a navigation menu: links in flyouts, each with a description. Zweihänder leaves that out: app navigation is a side or top navigation of links, which shows the current page; a flyout of described links is a marketing-site pattern. - **No item description.** Flyout items are Menu's entries, one line each. A second line of text is what a navigation menu needs, and it is not built. ## When to use Use a Menubar in a screen that works like a desktop tool, an invoice or report editor, a spreadsheet, where people look for commands by category and learn their shortcuts. Name each menu for what it holds and keep the order people know from desktop apps: File, Edit, View, then your own, then Help. } doCaption="Commands, grouped by the familiar File, Edit, View, with their shortcuts." dont={} dontCaption="Pages behind flyouts. Navigation belongs in a side or top navigation of links, where the current page shows." /> ## When not to use - **For the app's navigation.** Use a side or top navigation of [Links](?path=/docs/components-navigation-link--docs): it shows where the reader is, a menubar does not. - **For a few actions on one thing.** Use a [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) from a button, or Buttons. ## Accessibility - The bar is a `role="menubar"`, named by `aria-label`. Each trigger is a `menuitem` with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; a disabled menu's trigger has `aria-disabled`. - The bar is one tab stop. Arrow Left and Right move along the triggers, skipping disabled menus. - Arrow Down, Enter or Space on a trigger opens its flyout on the first item. Inside a flyout the keys are Menu's. - With a flyout open, Arrow Right and Left move to the next and previous menu and open it, and moving the pointer onto another trigger opens that menu instead. - Escape closes the flyout and returns focus to its trigger; choosing an action closes it too. - Shortcuts and icons are hidden from assistive tech; the label names the item. - Triggers are 24px tall; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) their hit area grows to 44px. - `isModal` (the default) makes the rest of the page inert while a flyout is open, so a screen reader stays in the menu.
