import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as PaginationStories from './Pagination.stories' # Pagination Moves through a long list one page at a time: previous, next, and the page numbers around the current one. Under a table it can also say which rows are shown ("21–40 of 340") and let the reader pick how many rows a page holds. ## Variants Pagination has one look and one size. What changes is how many numbers show, whether the pages are buttons or links, and the two optional ends. | Form | Use for | | --- | --- | | `getHref` | Pages with their own URL: each page is a link that can be opened in a new tab and shared. | | Buttons | Pages that only exist in this view's state, such as a filtered list in a dialog. The default. | | `totalItems` | A table footer, where the reader needs to know how many rows there are: adds the summary at the start. | | `pageSizeOptions` | Long tables where readers scan in bulk: adds a "Rows per page" select at the end. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Pagination } from 'zweihander/pagination' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/pagination.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Pagination.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Pagination.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/pagination](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/pagination) - Behaviour: a plain `
` around a list of buttons or links - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The first and last page always show, the current page keeps a sibling each side, and "…" appears only where it hides two or more pages. A single hidden page is shown instead, since "…" would take the same room. So the number of controls stays the same as you move through the middle, and Next does not jump. The summary and the select only appear when `totalItems` and `pageSizeOptions` are passed. The summary sits at the start and pushes the pages and the select to the end; on a narrow screen the row wraps. ## Measurements One size, Atlassian Design's: the `md` control tier (Foundations / Sizing), 32px. A control is square at its minimum; the inline padding only shows on a page number of three digits or more. Previous and next have no padding, so they stay square. The controls sit 4px apart, and the ellipsis has 8px either side. ## Color One colour set: the current page is the only fill. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. At rest a control has no fill. ## States - **Selected**: the current page is filled with `--color-background-brand-bold`, medium weight. It does not change on hover, and pressing it does nothing. - **Hover** fills a page, Previous or Next with an `--color-background-neutral` chip. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the control. - **Disabled**: Previous on the first page (above) and Next on the last, at 50% opacity. As buttons they are `disabled`; as links they lose their `href`. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
The rows-per-page select is a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs) at `size="sm"`, 32px: level with the page controls. Changing it moves to the page that holds the first row shown before, so the reader does not lose their place; it calls `onPageSizeChange`, then `onPageChange` if the page moved. `size` is deprecated. Pagination has one size, as Atlassian's does: `size="sm"` renders the same 32px controls as `md`. It is still accepted for one release; drop it. The kit's rule for a deprecated prop: it warns in the development console, once, when it is passed a value that is not its documented default (or when a renamed prop is used under its old name). So `size="sm"` warns, and `size="md"`, the default, is silent. Every other `
` attribute passes through. `paginationItems(page, total, siblings, boundary)` is exported too, for building your own. ## When to use Use Pagination under a long list or table when the reader needs to know where they are in it and jump to a page: search results, an audit log, an order history. Put it below the content it pages, and keep the list's position stable as pages change. Leave `siblingCount` and `boundaryCount` at 1. The control stays short and keeps the same width as the reader moves, so Next stays under the pointer. } doCaption="The default range: first, last, and the current page with a neighbour each side, on one line." dont={} dontCaption="Every page number at once wraps over several lines and buries the current page." /> Under a table, pass `totalItems` so the reader knows how much there is. The label sits under its marker, so every step gets the same width whatever its label. | | Vertical | Steps with long descriptions, or a narrow column beside the form. | | `sm` | Dense places: a dialog, a side panel. | | Bullets (`appearance="bullets"`) | A phone, a narrow dialog, or more steps than fit with labels: only the current step's label shows, "Step 3 of 4: Invite", over a row of dots. | | Navigable (`onStepClick`) | Flows where going back to fix an earlier step is normal. Finished steps become buttons. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Stepper } from 'zweihander/stepper' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/stepper.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Stepper.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Stepper.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/stepper](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/stepper) - Behaviour: a plain `
` around an ordered list - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The last step has no connector. Vertical, the connector runs down from each marker, beside the text. ## Measurements The marker's ring and the connector are 2px. The current dot's ring is 2px wide, 2px clear of the dot, in the dot's own colour. Horizontal, a connector runs along the markers' centre line from one marker to the next, `--space-2` clear of each. ## Color Complete and current share the primary colour: the filled disc says done, the ring says here. The current ring uses `--color-text-brand`, the step of the accent that reads at 4.5:1 on the page, because it frames a number. ## States A step's status is its state. With `onStepClick`, finished steps and the current one are buttons, with hover and focus of their own. }, { label: 'Clickable' }, { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' }, { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' }, ]} > - **Hover** underlines the label of a clickable step. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the step. - **Upcoming** steps are never buttons, so they have no hover or focus. - With bullets, **hover** fills the dot's hit area with `--color-background-neutral`, since there is no visible label to underline. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through. A step's `status` is only for the exception, such as an error: the rest is worked out from `current`. Only finished steps can be clicked; upcoming ones stay text, because a flow that can be skipped ahead is a set of Tabs. Bullets ignore `orientation` and draw no connectors: the dots sit close enough to read as one line. When `current` is past the last step, the "Step 3 of 4" line is left out. A step with an error that is also `current` keeps `aria-current` and the ring. ## When to use Use a Stepper when a task is split into a few steps that must be done in order, and it helps to know how many are left: checkout, onboarding, an import wizard. Keep it to three to five steps with a word or two each. } doCaption="Four steps, one word each: the whole flow at a glance." dont={} dontCaption="Ten steps squeeze every label and make the flow look longer than it is. Merge steps, or drop the stepper." /> ## When not to use - **For sections the reader can visit in any order.** Use [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs). - **For progress with no steps to name**, such as an upload. Use a [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs). - **For a single-page form.** Headings do the job; a stepper over one page promises steps that are not there. ## Accessibility - A `
` landmark named "Progress" around an ordered list: screen readers announce the number of steps and the position of each. - The current step has `aria-current="step"`. - The marker is decorative, so each label carries its status in visually hidden text: "Account, completed", "Invite, not started", "Workspace, has an error". Bullets hide every label but the current one, and still say each in the same hidden text. Their visible "Step 3 of 4: Invite" is hidden from screen readers, which hear the list instead. - An error on the current step keeps `aria-current="step"`. - Without `onStepClick` nothing is focusable. With it, complete and current steps are real buttons: reached with Tab, pressed with Enter or Space, showing the focus ring, and 44px tall on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`).

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as TabsStories from './Tabs.stories' # Tabs Switches between views of the same thing without leaving the page: Overview, Activity, Settings of one project. ## Variants `appearance` is the look. Either takes either size and orientation. | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | `underline` | The sections of a page or a panel. Tabs sit on a 1px rule; a bar slides under the selected one. The default. | | `pills` | A compact view switch in a toolbar, such as List / Board. A segmented track with the selected tab lifted. | | Form | Use for | | --- | --- | | `isFullWidth` | Two to four tabs that should fill a narrow container, such as a side panel or a phone screen. | | `vertical` | Many sections, or labels too long for a row: settings pages, a panel beside its content. | | Icons | Recognisable icons beside the label. Never an icon alone: the label is the tab's name. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Tabs } from 'zweihander/tabs' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tabs.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Tabs.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Tabs.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/tabs](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tabs) - Behaviour: [Base UI Tabs](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tabs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The indicator is one element for the whole list. It moves to the selected tab rather than each tab drawing its own, so a change of tab slides it across. ## Measurements Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing). `md` follows Atlassian Design's tabs: 32px tall, 8px inline padding, no gap between tabs, a 14/20 label and a 2px indicator as wide as the label (8px in from the tab's edges). The `underline` list is pulled out by those 8px, so the first label lines up with the content below it; inside a container that clips (a modal body, a card with hidden overflow) leave 8px of room on that side, or the first tab's focus ring is cut, as with Atlassian's. The 16px from the list to the panel is the kit's own: Atlassian leaves that to the panel's content. Atlassian Design has no small tab; `sm` is the kit's own, the same tab in a 24px box for dense panels. In `pills`, the track has a 2px inset and the chip's corner is the track's minus 2px, so the two stay concentric at every size. ## Color Each appearance has its own label colours and indicator. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. Pill labels use `--color-text-subtle`, not `--color-text-subtlest`: that is 4.3:1 on the `--color-background-neutral` track, under 4.5:1. ## States - **Selected**: the label takes the selected colour and the indicator slides under it (`underline`) or behind it (`pills`). - **Hover** brings an unselected label up to `--color-text`. It adds no fill. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline drawn just inside the tab, so it is not clipped by the list. - **Disabled** (Archive, above) is the enabled look at 50% opacity. It still takes focus. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
## When to use Use Tabs to split one thing into views the reader moves between freely, in any order: the overview, activity and settings of a project. Every panel is about the same object, and only one is needed at a time. Label each tab with a word or two. Labels do not wrap or shrink, so long ones push the row past its container. } doCaption="Short labels, a word or two: the row fits, and each reads at a glance." dont={} dontCaption="Long labels run past the edge of the container. Shorten them, or go vertical." /> Use `underline` for the sections of a page and `pills` for a view switch in a toolbar. Name the tab list with `aria-label` when no heading does. Selection is manual by default: arrow keys move focus, Enter or Space selects, so a slow panel does not load on every keypress. Turn on `activateOnFocus` only for light panels. ## When not to use - **For a sequence.** Steps that must be done in order belong in a Stepper. - **To compare content side by side.** Tabs show one panel at a time; put things that are read together on the same view. - **To go to another page.** Use links, a side navigation or Breadcrumbs: a tab changes the view, not the URL. - **For one setting with two or three options.** Use a radio group or a [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) group: that changes a value, not the view. ## Accessibility - `role="tablist"` of `role="tab"` buttons with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`; each panel is a `role="tabpanel"` labelled by its tab. - One tab stop: Tab moves into the list on the selected tab and the next Tab moves on to the panel. - Arrow keys move between tabs (Left and Right, or Up and Down when vertical, with `aria-orientation` set); Home and End jump to the ends. - Arrows move focus without selecting; Enter or Space selects. With `activateOnFocus`, arrows select as they go. - A disabled tab still takes focus, marked `aria-disabled`, so it is found and announced, but it cannot be selected. - Tabs are 24 or 32px tall and grow to 44px on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`). - Focus ring: 2px `--color-border-focused`, drawn inside the tab.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as AlertStories from './Alert.stories' # Alert A message about a page or a section that stays until the situation changes or the reader dismisses it: something went wrong, needs attention, or worked. ## Variants `variant` is the colour, by meaning; `appearance` is the emphasis. Any variant takes any appearance. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `info` | Something worth knowing that changes nothing: a plan change, scheduled maintenance. | | `success` | Something finished and stays true: a domain verified, an import done. | | `warning` | Something that will go wrong if nobody acts: a card expiring, a quota nearly used. | | `danger` | Something that went wrong and needs a next step: a failed upload, a lost connection. | | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | `subtle` | The default. Sits on the page without shouting. | | `outlined` | On a tinted or busy background, where a tint would disappear. | | `solid` | The one message nobody should miss, such as an outage banner. Rarely more than one per page. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Alert } from 'zweihander/alert' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/alert.json ``` - Source: [src/components/notifications/Alert.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/notifications/Alert.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/alert](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/alert) - Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Only the description is required. The icon is one line of body text tall, so it sits on the title's line. ## Measurements One size. The text is body text, so an alert sits in running content without a jump in size. The border is always there, 1px and transparent unless `outlined`, so switching appearance never moves the content. The padding counts that pixel: the content sits 16px from the alert's edge. The close button is 24px, flush with the padding and top-aligned with the icon. No shadow: an alert is part of the page. ## Color Each variant reads four tokens, the same four as a Tag of that variant, so the two always agree. Subtle and outlined keep the description in `--color-text`: a paragraph in the variant's colour is tiring to read, so the colour goes on the icon, the title and the close button. ## States The alert itself has no states. Its close button does. - **Hover** tints the close button with 15% of the alert's own text colour, so it reads on every variant and appearance. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, inside the button's edge. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through, including `ref`. ### Differences from the spec - **Sized after Atlassian's section message**: 16px padding, 16px from the icon to the text, 8px between title, description and actions, 8px corners, no shadow, a semibold 14/20 title, a 24px close button. - **Placed in the content, not at the top of the screen.** The spec describes a prominent message at the top; here an alert goes where the thing it is about is. An outage banner is a `solid` alert placed at the top by the page. - **Closing is the parent's job.** `onClose` reports the click and the alert stays until whoever rendered it removes it, so "dismissed" lives in your state and can be remembered across visits. ## When to use Use an Alert for a message about a page or a section that should stay put until it is dealt with: a failed save, a card about to expire, an import that finished. The title says what happened; the description says what it means and what to do. } doCaption="Say what happened and offer the next step." dont={} dontCaption="“Something went wrong” leaves the red box to do the talking, and the reader with nothing to do." /> The icon is decorative, so the variant has to be clear from the words too: "Upload failed", not just a red box. ## When not to use - **For news about something that just happened and needs nothing more.** Use a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs): it goes away by itself. - **For a one-line message under a form or a group of fields.** Use an [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs). - **For an error on one field.** Use the field's own `validationState` and `helperText`, tied to it with `aria-describedby`. - **For a decision the reader must make before going on.** Use a Modal. ## Accessibility - A plain `
` by default: an alert on the page when it loads is read in order, like the text around it, and does not interrupt. - An alert that **appears** in response to something (a failed save) needs `isLive`. `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are read at once; `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait for the screen reader to finish. - The icon is `aria-hidden`: the words carry the meaning. - The close button is a native `

An Alert can keep its message in `--color-text` because its box carries the colour; an inline alert has no box, so the text does. Every `--*-text` token is 4.5:1 on the page in both modes, so a message of any length stays readable. The action keeps its own colours: a Link or a Button, as passed. ## States The message has no states. An action in it has its own. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through, including `ref`. ## When to use Use an Inline Alert for a short message about the thing right above it: a group of fields, a whole form, a section. A failed submit is the common case. } doCaption="An error about one field goes on the field, as its helper text: it is read when the field is focused." dont={} dontCaption="An inline alert under a field is not tied to it: a screen reader in the field never hears it." /> ## When not to use - **For an error on one field.** Use the field's own `validationState` and `helperText`, tied to it with `aria-describedby`. - **For a message about a whole page or region**, or one that needs a title, an action row or a close button. Use an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-alert--docs). - **For news about something that just happened.** Use a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs). ## Accessibility - A plain `
` by default, read in order with the page. - `isLive` for a message that appears in response to something (a failed submit): `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are read at once, `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait. - The icon is `aria-hidden`: the words carry the meaning. - The action is whatever you pass (a Link, a Button) and keeps its own keyboard behaviour and focus ring.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as ToastStories from './Toast.stories' # Toast A short message in a corner of the screen about something that just happened: saved, sent, moved, failed. It closes itself after a few seconds and never blocks the page. Try it: the toast opens in the corner of this window. ## Variants `variant` colours the icon only; the message stays in the surface's text colour. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `neutral` | Most toasts: something done, nothing to judge. "File moved to Trash." | | `info` | A neutral fact about what just happened: "Sync paused while offline." | | `success` | A result worth confirming because it was not obvious: "Invite sent to 12 people." | | `warning` | Done, with a catch: "Saved, but 2 rows were skipped." | | `danger` | Something failed. Interrupts the screen reader. Say what to do next, and keep the way to do it on the page too. | `promise()` adds a loading toast that becomes `success` or `danger` when the promise settles. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { ToastProvider, useToast } from 'zweihander/toast' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/toast.json ``` - Source: [src/components/notifications/Toast.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/notifications/Toast.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/toast](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/toast) - Behaviour: [Base UI Toast](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toast) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Only the title, or the description alone, is required. The icon box is one line of body text tall, so it sits on the title's line. ## Measurements One size. Toasts stack with a gap, the newest nearest the edge they grow from. At most 25rem (400px) wide, and never wider than the window less the edge distance on both sides. The padding counts the 1px border: the content sits 16px from the toast's edge. The close button is 24px, top-aligned with the content and flush with the padding, 16px from the text. The action is a 24px row straight under the description. ## Color The toast takes the page's own appearance: the overlay surface, its border and the overlay shadow lift it off what is under it. `neutral` shows no icon. ## States }, ]} > - **Hover** fills the close button with `--color-background-neutral`. Hovering the stack also pauses every toast's timer. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline inside the action or the close button. Focus in the stack pauses the timers too. - **Pending** is a `promise()` toast: a spinner in place of the icon, and no timer until it settles. - **Entering** fades in and slides `--space-2` from the edge the stack grows from; **leaving** fades out. With reduced motion, only the fade. ## API `ToastProvider` wraps the app once: {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`useToast()`, anywhere inside it, shows and closes toasts: ```tsx const toast = useToast() toast.add({ title: 'File moved to Trash', action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: restore } }) ``` {/* Markdown tables do not scroll by themselves on a phone either. */}
| `useToast()` | | | --- | --- | | `add(options)` | Shows a toast, returns its id. | | `update(id, options)` | Changes one in place; only the options given change. | | `close(id?)` | Closes one, or all. | | `promise(promise, { loading, success, error })` | A loading toast that becomes success or danger when the promise settles. | | Option | Values | | | --- | --- | --- | | `title`, `description` | node | | | `variant` | `neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` | `neutral` | | `action` | `{ label, onClick }` | One button. | | `timeout` | number (ms) | The provider's by default. `0` keeps it until dismissed. | | `priority` | `low`, `high` | `high` by default for `danger`. | | `onClose` | function | |
### Differences from the spec - **Sized after Atlassian's flag**: 400px wide, 16px padding, 16px from the icon to the text, 8px from the title to the description, 8px corners, the overlay shadow, a 24px close button. The stack sits 16px from the window edge, where Atlassian's sits 48px up and 80px in: that offset clears its own navigation, and the kit's stack can sit on any edge. - **Bottom right by default**, where the spec suggests top right. `placement` takes any corner or edge centre. ## When to use Use a Toast to confirm something the reader just did, when the result is not already visible: moved, sent, copied, saved in the background. Offer "Undo" when it can be undone. } doCaption="News about something just done, with a way to undo it. Undo is also reachable from the Trash." dont={} dontCaption="A problem the reader has to fix goes away in a few seconds. Put it in an Alert on the page." /> Keep it to a few words. A toast is read in passing, often half-noticed. ## When not to use - **For something the reader must act on, or might need to read twice.** Use an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-alert--docs) on the page, or a Modal for a decision. - **For an error in a form.** Use the field's own error, or an [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs) under the form. - **As the only way to an action.** The toast goes away; the same action ("Undo") must be reachable somewhere else. - **To confirm what is already visible.** A row that appears in a table needs no "Row added" toast. ## Accessibility - The stack is a polite live region: a new toast is announced without interrupting. `danger` toasts (and any with `priority: 'high'`) are `role="alertdialog"` and announced at once. - Each toast is a non-modal dialog named by its title, or by its description when it has none (as `promise()` toasts do). - A toast closes after 5 seconds by default (the provider's `timeout`); `timeout: 0` keeps it until it is dismissed. At most three show at once (`limit`). - Timers pause while the pointer is over the stack or focus is in it, so there is time to reach the action. F6 moves focus to the stack. - The close button is named `Dismiss`; Enter and Space press it. On touch screens its hit area grows to 44×44px, and a toast swipes away toward the nearest edge. - A toast raised from inside a modal shows above it and is not hidden from assistive tech by it.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as ConfirmDialogStories from './ConfirmDialog.stories' # Confirm Dialog Asks before something that cannot be undone: a warning, the action as a question, what it will destroy, then Cancel or the action. A press outside does nothing, so the reader has to choose. ## Variants | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | Default | An everyday delete: a comment, a file, a saved view. One question, two buttons. | | Non-destructive (`kind="default"`) | A decision that destroys nothing: sign out everywhere, leave without saving. No warning icon, and the action is a primary button. | | Type to confirm (`confirmText`) | A large delete that cannot be undone: a workspace, an account, a project with its files. The action waits until the reader types the name. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { ConfirmDialog } from 'zweihander/confirm-dialog' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/confirm-dialog.json ``` - Source: [src/components/overlays/ConfirmDialog.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/ConfirmDialog.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/modal](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/modal) (the alert dialog) - Built on: [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs) with `isAlert`, on [Base UI Alert Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The open dialogs on this tab and the next are pictures: rendered in a frame with `container` and `isModal={false}`, inert, so they do not lock this page or take its focus. ## Measurements It is a Modal at `size="sm"` (at most 400px wide): container, title, body and footer take Modal's measurements, except the 16px from the title to the description (8px in a Modal). Its own parts: The icon is one line of the title tall, so it stays on the first line when the title wraps. ## Color Everything else takes Modal's colours, and the buttons keep their own: Cancel is `secondary` outlined, the action `destructive` (`primary` with `kind="default"`, which has no warning icon). ## States The dialog is open or closed. With `confirmText`, the action is disabled until the field matches, then enabled; without it, it is enabled from the start. }, { label: 'Ready', content: }, ]} /> ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
### Differences from the spec - **Destructive by default.** `kind="default"` drops the warning icon and makes the action primary; for anything more custom, use a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs) with `isAlert`, where you choose the buttons. - **No pending state.** The dialog closes on confirm. If the delete can fail, control `open` and keep it open until your request settles. ## When to use Before an action that destroys something the reader cannot get back. Put the object's name in the title, say in the description what goes with it, and name the action button after what it does. Type to confirm is for the few deletes that are both large and final. Used on every delete, it becomes a chore readers do without reading. } doCaption="Ask once for an everyday delete, with the action on the button." dont={} dontCaption="Do not make the reader type for a small delete: it teaches them to type without reading." /> ## When not to use - **When the action can be undone.** Do it, then offer Undo in a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs): no question is faster than a good one. - **For a decision that destroys nothing**, such as Sign out or Leave without saving. Use a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs) with `isAlert`. - **To show a warning.** Use an [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs). ## Accessibility - `role="alertdialog"`, named by the title (the icon is hidden from assistive tech) and described by the consequence. - Focus starts on Cancel, so Enter on open cannot delete. With `confirmText` it starts in the field, which is named "To confirm, type" and the name. - The action stays disabled until the field matches exactly, case included; spaces around the text are ignored. Enter in the field confirms once it matches. - A press outside does nothing. Cancel and Escape close it without confirming, and focus goes back to the trigger. - Reopened, the field starts empty.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as ModalStories from './Modal.stories' # Modal A dialog over the page that has to be dealt with before going back: a short form, a confirmation, a decision. Everything behind it is dimmed and out of reach until it closes. ## Variants | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | Dialog (default) | A short task on its own: edit a profile, invite people. A close button, Escape and a press on the backdrop all close it. | | Alert (`isAlert`) | A decision with consequences: delete, discard, leave. No close button and a press on the backdrop does nothing, so it ends only through its own buttons or Escape. | `size` sets the maximum width: `sm` (400px) for an alert, `md` (600px) for a short form, `lg` (800px) for long content. Taller than the screen, the body scrolls and the title and footer stay in view. On a screen under 480px wide the modal is the whole screen. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Modal, ModalClose } from 'zweihander/modal' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/modal.json ``` - Source: [src/components/overlays/Modal.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Modal.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/modal](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/modal) - Behaviour: [Base UI Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog) and [Alert Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The open modals on this tab and the next are pictures: real modals rendered in a frame with `container`, not modal (`isModal={false}`) and inert, so they do not lock this page or take its focus. ## Measurements The gutter to the screen has no token: the spacing scale has no 60px step, so the CSS adds two (`--space-12` and `--space-3`). | Screen width | Gutter, each side | From the top | Width | Height | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 480px and up | 60px | 60px | `size`, at most the screen less 120px | Its content, at most the screen less 120px; then the body scrolls | | Under 480px | 0 | 0 | The screen | The screen; the body scrolls, the footer sits at the bottom | "Screen" is the box the modal opens in: the window, or the `container` when that contains layout. Under 480px the modal has no corner radius and no shadow. Width is `size`: at most 400px (`sm`), 600px (`md`) or 800px (`lg`), set in rem (25, 37.5, 50), and never wider than the screen less its gutter. These are Atlassian's small, medium and large modals, with its 24px padding, 12px corner and 20/24 semibold title, 16px from the title to the body and from the body to the footer, and 8px between the footer's buttons. The 8px from the title to the description is the kit's own: Atlassian's header has no description. The 60px gutter, the 60px from the top (the modal is not centred, so a body that grows does not move the title) and the full screen under 480px are Atlassian's too. The header stacks the title and the description in one column, with the close button beside both. The close button is a 24px box, as tall as the title's line, flush with the padding. The border is 1px, and the padding counts it: the content sits 24px from the modal's edge. Backdrop and modal sit on the `--layer-overlay` layer and fade in over `--duration-base`. ## Color Buttons in the footer keep their own colours: see Button. ## States The modal is open or closed. Opening fades the backdrop in and scales the container up from 97%; closing reverses it. The close button is the only part with states of its own: - **Hover** fills the button with `--color-background-neutral`. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline drawn inside the button, so it is not clipped at the container's corner. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`ModalClose` closes the modal it is in. Give it your own button with `render`: `}>Cancel`. ## When to use Reach for a modal last: it stops everything else. Use one when the task must be finished or abandoned before going on, or for a decision with consequences. For a decision, use `isAlert`, say exactly what will happen in the description, and name the buttons after what they do. Before a delete or anything else that cannot be undone, use a [Confirm Dialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirm-dialog--docs): it is this alert with the warning, the focus on Cancel and type to confirm built in. } doCaption="Name the buttons after what they do: Delete, Keep project. The choice reads without the question." dont={} dontCaption="OK and Cancel make the reader go back to the question to know which one deletes." /> Put the main action last in the footer, and dismiss actions (Cancel, Keep) in the `secondary` variant. ## When not to use - **For a small form tied to one button**, such as Share or a filter. Use a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs): it opens beside the button and leaves the page usable. - **For information**: a success, a warning, a tip. Use an [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs) or a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs); neither stops the reader. - **For a long or many-step task.** Give it a page of its own. - **Over another modal.** Close the first, or move the second step into it. ## Accessibility - `role="dialog"` (or `alertdialog`), named by the title and described by the description. - Opening moves focus to the first focusable element, or `initialFocus`, and traps it inside. The page behind is `aria-hidden`, its pointer events are blocked by the backdrop, and its scroll is locked. Closing returns focus to the trigger. - `isModal={false}` drops the focus trap, the scroll lock and the hidden page, but the backdrop still covers the page. It is for pictures of a modal, such as the ones on these tabs: a real modal stays modal. - Escape closes it, as does a press outside unless `isAlert` or `closeOnBackdropClick={false}`. An alert dialog closes only through its own buttons (and Escape). - **One layer with the popups.** Modal, Popover, Select and Combobox all sit at `--layer-overlay`. Each portals to the end of `` when it opens, so the most recent is on top: a Select opened inside a modal lists its options above the modal, which a higher modal layer would hide. - The close button is named `Close` (`closeLabel`), has the 2px focus ring and a 44px hit area on touch screens.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as PopoverStories from './Popover.stories' # Popover A small panel anchored to a button, for content you interact with: a share form, a filter, a set of options. It opens on click and stays until you close it. ## Variants | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | Non-modal (default) | Most popovers. Tab can leave it and the page stays usable while it is open. | | Modal (`isModal`) | A popover that must be finished or closed first: focus stays inside, the page does not scroll and presses outside are blocked. | | `openOnHover` | A preview that also opens on hover, when what it holds must be reachable by click, keyboard and touch. A person or record preview on a link fits here too. | A title is optional. Without one, name the popover with `aria-label`: ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Popover } from 'zweihander/popover' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/popover.json ``` - Source: [src/components/overlays/Popover.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Popover.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/popover](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/popover) - Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The open popovers on this tab and the next are pictures: real popovers rendered in place with `container` and inert, the popup laid out under the trigger where it opens. ## Measurements The container is as wide as its content, at most 22rem and never wider than the room beside the trigger. It has no arrow: it opens 6px from the trigger and lines up with it, which already ties the two. It has a 1px border and a semibold title. The header stacks the title and the description with no gap between them, and the close button sits beside both, flush in the top-right corner of the padding. The 8px corner and the overlay shadow are Atlassian's popup; the 16px padding and the 22rem cap are the kit's own. The close button is 20px: 2px around its icon, one line of text tall. Popovers sit on the `--layer-overlay` layer and fade in over `--duration-fast`. ## Color Select and Combobox lists use the same surface: `--color-surface-overlay`, its border and shadow. ## States The popover is open or closed. Opening fades it in and scales it up from 97%, from the trigger's side. The trigger keeps the states of its own component (see Button); the close button is the only part with states of its own: - **Hover** fills the close button with `--color-background-neutral`. - **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline drawn inside the button. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
## When to use Use a Popover for a short task that belongs to the button that opens it: share a file, set a filter, pick from a few options. It holds links, inputs and buttons, which a Tooltip must not. } doCaption="A short task tied to its button: one field and one action." dont={} dontCaption="A whole form in a popover. It closes on a stray press outside and loses the work: use a Modal." /> It opens below the trigger by default; `side` and `align` move it. When that side has no room, it flips to the other one. ## When not to use - **For a label or a hint** on hover or focus. Use a [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs). - **For a list of actions or commands.** Use a [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs): it has the arrow-key navigation a list of commands needs. - **For a long form or a decision with consequences.** Use a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs). ## Accessibility - The popup is a `role="dialog"` named by `title` (or `aria-label`) and described by `description`. The trigger carries `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup`. - Opening moves focus into the popup; Escape or a press outside closes it and returns focus to the trigger. - **Non-modal by default:** Tab can leave the popup, and the page stays usable. `isModal` switches to Base UI's modal mode: focus is trapped, page scroll is locked and presses outside are blocked. - Base UI only traps focus when the popup contains a close button, and a touch screen reader needs one to get out. So a modal popover without `hasCloseButton` still renders one: hidden until it has keyboard focus, then shown in the corner, so focus is never invisible. - `openOnHover` adds hover to click, it does not replace it: the content stays reachable by keyboard and touch. - The close button has the 2px focus ring and a 44px hit area on touch screens.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as TooltipStories from './Tooltip.stories' # Tooltip A short label that appears when you hover over or focus a control: the name of an icon-only button, a keyboard shortcut, a one-line hint. ## Variants | Variant | When to use | |---|---| | Tooltip | A label or a one-line hint on a control. | The tooltip opens on hover after a short delay and on keyboard focus at once. Wrap a row of tooltips in `TooltipGroup` so that once one has opened, moving to the next opens it without the delay: Only one tooltip is open at a time: opening one closes any other. Hover or focus the triggers above to see them. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Tooltip, TooltipGroup } from 'zweihander/tooltip' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tooltip.json ``` - Source: [src/components/overlays/Tooltip.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Tooltip.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/tooltip](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tooltip) - Behaviour: [Base UI Tooltip](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The open tooltips on this tab and the next are pictures: real tooltips held open and rendered in place with `container`, laid out above the trigger where they open. ## Measurements The container is as wide as its text, at most 240px (15rem) and never wider than the room beside the trigger; longer text wraps. It opens 6px from the trigger, on the `--layer-tooltip` layer, above popovers and modals, so a tooltip on a control inside one still shows. It fades in over `--duration-fast`. ## Color The tooltip is inverted in both modes: a tooltip is not part of the page, and the dark-on-light (light-on-dark in dark mode) box says so, at the same contrast as body text. ## States }, { label: 'Open', content: }, ]} /> - **Closed** until the pointer rests on the trigger for `delay` (300ms), or the trigger takes keyboard focus, which opens it at once. - **Open** until Escape, blur or the pointer leaves, after `closeDelay`. Opening fades it in and scales it up from 96%. - The trigger keeps the states of its own component; the tooltip has none of its own. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`TooltipGroup` is Base UI's `Tooltip.Provider`: tooltips inside it share one delay. ## When to use Use a Tooltip for a label or a hint: the name of an icon-only button, a keyboard shortcut, one line on what a control does. 300ms before it opens is quick enough to feel responsive and long enough that tooltips do not flash as the pointer crosses a toolbar. } doCaption="A short label that repeats the icon-only button's name for sighted users." dont={} dontCaption="Rules the reader needs to fill the field. Touch cannot open a tooltip, and it hides as soon as focus moves on: put the rules under the field." /> It opens on the `side` given, top by default. When that side has no room, it flips to the other one. ## When not to use - **For anything a reader needs to finish a task.** Put it on the page: a tooltip cannot be reached by touch, and it disappears the moment you look away. - **For links, buttons or other interactive content.** Hover and touch cannot reach the tooltip. Use a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs). - **For a rich preview.** A tooltip holds text only. Use a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs) with `openOnHover`. - **On a disabled button.** It is not focusable, so its tooltip never opens by keyboard. Put the reason it is disabled in text next to it. ## Accessibility - It opens on hover after `delay` and on keyboard focus at once, and closes on Escape, blur or pointer leave. - Base UI keeps tooltips out of the accessibility tree. This component gives the popup `role="tooltip"` and, while it is open, points the trigger's `aria-describedby` at it, so it is read as a description. - It is a **description, not a name.** An icon-only button still needs its own `aria-label`; the tooltip then shows that label to sighted users too. - The trigger must be focusable: a Button, a link, a field. - `--color-surface` on `--color-text` reads at 16:1 or more in both modes.

components-states-emptystate--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as EmptyStateStories from './EmptyState.stories' # Empty State What a list, a table or a page shows when there is nothing in it yet: why it is empty, and what to do about it. ## Variants There are three kinds of empty, and they need three kinds of copy. The component is the same; the words and the action are not. | Kind | Use for | | --- | --- | | First use | Nothing has been made yet. Say what will live here, and offer the way in: "No projects yet", New project. | | No results | A search or a filter matched nothing. Say what was searched, and offer to clear it: "No projects match", Clear search. | | Cleared out | Everything is done. Often no action at all: "All caught up". | `size="sm"` fits a panel or a table body; `md` fills a page or a section. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { EmptyState } from 'zweihander/empty-state' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/empty-state.json ``` - Source: [src/components/states/EmptyState.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/states/EmptyState.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/empty-state](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/empty-state) - Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Only the title is required. [Error State](?path=/docs/components-states-errorstate--docs) and [Success State](?path=/docs/components-states-successstate--docs) are this layout with the disc in their own tone. ## Measurements The icon is half the disc's size. Title and description are at most 464px wide at `md` and 304px at `sm` (29rem and 19rem, Atlassian's wide and narrow empty state), so they stay a short paragraph on a wide page. `md` keeps Atlassian's rhythm: 48px above and below, 24px under the image, 16px under the heading, 24px above the buttons, 8px between them. `sm` keeps the 16px and 24px and is 16px under a smaller image. ## Color One tone: neutral. Switch the theme in the toolbar: the values follow. The container has no fill: it takes the surface it sits on. ## States Empty State itself is static: it has no hover, focus or pressed look. Its action does, and those are the action's own (here, an outlined Button). ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through, including `ref`. ## When to use Use an Empty State wherever a list, a table or a page can have nothing in it: before the first item is made, after a search matches nothing, when everything is done. Write the title for the reader's situation, and give them the next step. } doCaption="Say what is empty and what will live here, and offer the way in." dont={} dontCaption="“No data” says neither why nor what to do next." /> ## When not to use - **When loading failed.** Use an [Error State](?path=/docs/components-states-errorstate--docs): "No projects" when the request failed tells the reader their work is gone. - **When a flow has finished.** Use a [Success State](?path=/docs/components-states-successstate--docs). - **While content is loading.** Use a Skeleton or a Spinner: an empty state shown before the data arrives flashes the wrong message. ## Accessibility - The title is a real heading, so a screen reader user jumping by headings finds out the area is empty. Set `headingLevel` to fit the outline: `3` inside a section headed by an `h2`. - The icon is `aria-hidden`; the title has to say it all. - It is not a live region, so it is not announced when it replaces results. If a search updates as you type, announce the count elsewhere, in a `role="status"` line such as "0 results".

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as ErrorStateStories from './ErrorState.stories' # Error State What a list, a panel or a page shows when loading it failed: what went wrong, and a way forward, usually "Try again". ## Variants | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | With details | A failure support may need to trace: an error code or request id under the description, selected in one click. | | Default title | The last resort, for a failure you cannot describe: "Something went wrong". | | `sm` | A panel, a card or a table body that failed on its own while the rest of the page loaded. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { ErrorState } from 'zweihander/error-state' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/error-state.json ``` - Source: [src/components/states/ErrorState.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/states/ErrorState.tsx) - Spec: our own; uiguideline.com has no page for it - Behaviour: built on [Empty State](?path=/docs/components-states-emptystate--docs), no Base UI part - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Empty State's parts, with the disc in the danger tone, plus details under the description. ## Measurements Empty State's, plus the details line. ## Color One tone: danger, on the disc and the details line. The title and description stay neutral, so the page does not shout. `--color-text-danger` on `--color-background-danger` is 4.5:1 or more in both modes. ## States Error State itself is static. Its action has the states of its own Button. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through, including `ref`. ## When to use Use an Error State in place of content that failed to load: a list, a panel, a whole page. Say what failed in the reader's words, say that nothing is lost when that is true, and offer a way forward. } doCaption="Say what failed, that nothing is lost, and offer to try again." dont={} dontCaption="A raw error is for developers, and with no action the reader is stuck." /> Details are for support, not for the reader: keep them small and selectable so they can be pasted into a message. ## When not to use - **When there is simply nothing there.** Use an [Empty State](?path=/docs/components-states-emptystate--docs). - **When an action failed but the screen is fine**, such as a save. Use an Alert or a Toast and keep the reader's work on screen. - **For a field's error.** Show it on the field, through its own error message. ## Accessibility - The title is a real heading, as on Empty State. Set `headingLevel` to fit the outline. - The icon is `aria-hidden`; the title says what failed. - `isLive` makes it a `role="alert"`: use it when the error replaces content that was loading, so a screen reader hears that it failed. Without it, nothing is announced.
